Q537CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q21NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases to form a meaningful sentence:
(A) that true science fiction
(B) is a creation of
(C) I have often made the point
(D) the last two centuries

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D)
  2. (C), (A), (B), (D)
  3. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (C), (B), (D), (A)
Concept to recallMain clause first; “the point that …” introduces its content clause.
  1. C “I have often made the point” + A “that true science fiction”.
  2. + B “is a creation of” + D “the last two centuries” ⇒ C A B D.

Answer: option (2) — (C), (A), (B), (D)

Q538CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q29NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases to form a meaningful sentence:
(A) following the guidelines of the Supreme Court,
(B) I appeal to the people of Delhi,
(C) as responsible citizens,
(D) to burn only green crackers

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
  1. (B), (D), (C), (A)
  2. (B), (C), (D), (A)
  3. (A), (B), (C), (D)
  4. (C), (D), (B), (A)
Concept to recallAn introductory participle phrase ending in a comma (“Following …,”) opens the sentence; keep a modifier next to the noun it describes.
  1. A ends with a comma and gives the basis of the appeal ⇒ it opens the sentence.
  2. B “I appeal to the people of Delhi,” + C “as responsible citizens,” (describes the people).
  3. D “to burn only green crackers” completes “appeal to … to burn” ⇒ A B C D.

Answer: option (3) — (A), (B), (C), (D)

TrapOption 2 (B C D A) is also a possible sentence, but it leaves “following the guidelines” trailing after “crackers”, where it seems to describe the crackers.
Q539CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q4NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases to form a meaningful sentence:
(A) actions of characters and dialogues
(B) intended to be
(C) a drama is a composition in prose or verse
(D) acted on stage through

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (C), (B), (D), (A)
  2. (A), (B), (C), (D)
  3. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (D), (B), (C), (A)
Concept to recallBegin with the definition’s subject + verb; “intended to be” needs a participle; “through” needs its object.
  1. C “a drama is a composition in prose or verse”.
  2. + B “intended to be” + D “acted on stage through”.
  3. + A “actions of characters and dialogues” ⇒ C B D A.

Answer: option (1) — (C), (B), (D), (A)

Q540CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q7NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases to form a meaningful sentence:
(A) and saw her son in a blue shirt
(B) she came to the balcony
(C) surging on the rocking horse
(D) hearing some sound suddenly

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (D), (B), (A), (C)
  2. (A), (B), (D), (C)
  3. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (C), (B), (D), (A)
Concept to recallCause → action → what she saw; a participle phrase sits next to the noun it describes.
  1. D “hearing some sound suddenly,” (cause) + B “she came to the balcony”.
  2. A “and saw her son in a blue shirt” + C “surging on the rocking horse” (describes the son).
  3. ⇒ D B A C.

Answer: option (1) — (D), (B), (A), (C)

Q541CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q13NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases into a meaningful sentence. The beginning of the sentence has been given below. Read the options and find out which of the four combinations is correct:
The need for a scientific understanding…
(A) the Rio Earth Summit, the first of its kind
(B) involving world leaders on environment and development
(C) of natural ecosystems including forests was the main objective of
(D) of phenomena like climate change, biodiversity, and conservation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (C), (D), (A), (B)
  2. (B), (C), (D), (A)
  3. (D), (C), (A), (B)
  4. (D), (B), (A), (C)
Concept to recallPara-jumble: attach each fragment to the one it grammatically needs (“understanding of”, “objective of + noun”).
  1. “understanding” needs “of”: D “of phenomena like climate change …”.
  2. C adds a second object “of natural ecosystems … was the main objective of”.
  3. C ends in “of” ⇒ A “the Rio Earth Summit, the first of its kind”.
  4. B “involving world leaders” describes the summit ⇒ D C A B.

Answer: option (3) — (D), (C), (A), (B)

TrapC-first also starts with “of”, but then D would dangle after “objective of”.
Q542CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q14NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases into a meaningful sentence. The beginning of the sentence has been given below. Read the options and find out which of the four combinations is correct:
The point is that both ecology and resource management science…
(A) and mechanistic worldview,  shaped by the utilitarian premise
(B) of the industrial age, had more to say
(C) about the human mission to extract rather than to conserve
(D) that developed under the conventional

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  2. (D), (A), (C), (B)
  3. (D), (A), (B), (C)
  4. (C), (D), (B), (A)
Concept to recallFind the subject’s relative clause, then the verb, then its complement.
  1. Subject “science” + relative clause: D “that developed under the conventional”.
  2. “conventional” + A “and mechanistic worldview, shaped by the utilitarian premise”.
  3. “premise” + B “of the industrial age, had more to say” (main verb).
  4. “say” + C “about the human mission …” ⇒ D A B C.

Answer: option (3) — (D), (A), (B), (C)

Q543CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q15NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases into a meaningful sentence. The beginning of the sentence has been given below. Read the options and find out which of the four combinations is correct:

  2. (A), (C), (B), (D)
  3. (C), (D), (B), (A)
  4. (A), (B), (D), (C)
Concept to recall“like” introduces examples (nouns); the main clause then needs subject + verb + object.
  1. “factors like” + C “globalization, and the” + D “hegemony of English”.
  2. Main clause: B “the language communities cannot shirk” (subject + verb).
  3. “shirk” needs an object: A “their responsibility …” ⇒ C D B A.

Answer: option (3) — (C), (D), (B), (A)

TrapOption 1 puts the object (A) before its verb (B).

  1. Subject: D “the pollutants from the factory”.
  2. Verb: B “had percolated into the underground water”.
  3. Result: C “thus causing a water crisis” + A “in the region” ⇒ D B C A.

Q549CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q1NTA final key
Re-arrange the following phrases in the right sequence to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) for seven hours but was hardly
(B) because of the absence of any motivation
(C) able to decide who the murderer was
(D) she worked on the case
  1. (A), (C), (D), (B)
  2. (D), (A), (C), (B)
  3. (D), (C), (B), (A)
  4. (A), (B), (C), (D)
Concept to recallPara jumble: find the subject/opening (a part that can stand first), then chain the parts by grammar — an article or preposition at the end of one part needs its object at the start of the next.
  1. (D) she worked on the case has the subject and main verb, so it opens.
  2. (A) for seven hours but was hardly continues the time phrase; hardly must be followed by (C) able to decide who the murderer was.
  3. (B) because of the absence of any motivation gives the reason and closes the sentence: D-A-C-B.
  4. Options starting with (A) begin with a dangling for seven hours without a subject.

Answer: option (2) — (D), (A), (C), (B)

Q594CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 2 · Q12NTA final key
Passage (summarised): from The God of Small Things (Arundhati Roy), ch. 1

It is raining when Rahel returns to Ayemenem; the rain falls in “slanting silver ropes” that plough up the loose earth. The old house on the hill wears its steep, gabled roof like a low hat; its mossy walls are soft and bulging with damp. The overgrown garden is full of the whisper and scurry of small lives: a rat snake rubs itself on a glistening stone, bullfrogs cruise the scummy pond, a drenched mongoose crosses the driveway.

The house looks empty — doors and windows locked, verandah bare — but the sky-blue Plymouth is still parked outside, and inside Baby Kochamma (Navomi Ipe, Rahel’s grandfather’s younger sister, her baby grand-aunt) is still alive. Rahel has not come to see her, though; she has come to see her brother Estha. They are two-egg (“dizygotic”) twins, Estha the elder by eighteen minutes. They never looked alike, so relatives and the Syrian Orthodox bishops who visited the Ayemenem House for donations never asked “which is which?”; the confusion lay somewhere deeper.

Arrange the following sentences in order of its occurrence in the given passage :
(A) The doors and windows were locked
(B) A rat snake rubbed itself against a glistening store
(C) Slanting silver ropes slammed into loose earth
(D) The wild overgrown garden was full of the whisper and scurry of small lives
(E) Syrian Orthodox bishops who frequently visited the Ayemenem House for donations.
Choose the correct order :
  1. (B), (C), (D), (E), (A)
  2. (C), (D), (B), (A), (E)
  3. (E), (A), (B), (D), (C)
  4. (D), (A), (C), (B), (E)
Concept to recallOrder-of-occurrence: find which detail comes first (the rain), then trace the description outward.
  1. The passage opens with the rain (C).
  2. Then the garden full of small lives (D), and inside it the rat snake (B).
  3. Then the house with locked doors (A), and last the bishops (E) in the twins’ paragraph.
  4. C, D, B, A, E — option (2). Only (2) begins with (C).

Answer: option (2) — (C), (D), (B), (A), (E)

Q598CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q11NTA final key
Passage (summarised): blackberry picking with grandparents

As a child of seven or eight, the narrator went blackberry picking with his grandparents in late August, when the berries were ripe. Grandad drove them in his old van — uncomfortable and not very safe, but it had a character no sleek new car could match, and the boy enjoyed bouncing along.

They always went to the same spot, where wild bushes lined the road as far as the eye could see; the road overlooked a small pitch-and-putt course where golfers “ambled sedately” from hole to hole.

They picked for hours. Nana warned him not to eat any berries before washing them but turned a blind eye as he gorged; he liked the bitter unripe red ones, but the green ones were too much even for him. By evening Grandad hauled a half-full bin bag back to the van, juice dripping; Nana would later make apple and blackberry tarts and jam. The boy’s stomach hurt, his hands stung from thorn pricks and were stained dark purple — and he always enjoyed those days.

Arrange the sentences in its order of occurrence :
(A) Nana warned me not to eat any until they had all been washed but turned a knowing blind eye while I gorged anyway.
(B) I always enjoyed a trip as we bounced along to our destination.
(C) The road overlooked a small pitch and putt course.
(D) Nana would later make apple and blackberry tarts.
(E) Grandad’s van had a character you would not find in a sleek new car.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (B), (E), (A), (C), (D)
  2. (C), (B), (E), (A), (D)
  3. (E), (B), (C), (A), (D)
  4. (D), (A), (E), (B), (C)
Concept to recallNarrative order follows the day: the drive, the spot, the picking, the evening.
  1. The van (E), then the bumpy trip (B) — paragraph 1.
  2. The spot overlooking the golf course (C), the picking with Nana’s warning (A), the tarts later (D).
  3. E-B-C-A-D.

Answer: option (3) — (E), (B), (C), (A), (D)

Q599CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q20NTA final key
Re arrange the jumbled sentences into a paragraph.
(A) With the advent of new technology, the film makers had the possibility of synchronising the sound track with action.
(B) The movies were called talkies since the audience was able to hear the actors talk with each other.
(C) This included Dialogues, Music and Special effects.
(D) Films used to be silent with just action on the screen along with subtitles.
(E) However colour movies were somewhat slow due to the processing cost.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D), (E)
  2. (D), (A), (C), (B), (E)
  3. (C), (B), (D), (A), (B)
  4. (B), (A),(D), (E), (C)
Concept to recallChronology plus pronoun links: ‘This’ in (C) needs an antecedent (the soundtrack in A).
  1. Start in the past: silent films (D).
  2. New technology synchronised sound (A); ‘This included dialogue, music …’ (C).
  3. So films became ‘talkies’ (B); ‘However’ colour came slowly (E). D-A-C-B-E.

Answer: option (2) — (D), (A), (C), (B), (E)

Q600CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q21NTA final key
Rearrange the jumbled sentences into a paragraph.
(A) Thousands of people lost their homes, lives and were displaced.
(B) Chennai was flooded after incessant rains in November 2022 following the worst rainfall in 100 years.
(C) The Indian Army, Navy and Air Force worked shoulder to shoulder with many NGOs.
(D) Hectic rescue efforts were on, round the clock.
(E) Many areas were completely submerged in water causing massive damage to life and supply.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D), (E)
  2. (E), (D), (C), (B), (A)
  3. (B), (E), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (E), (B), (D), (A), (C)
Concept to recallEvent → extent → human cost → response → who responded.
  1. The event (B), then submerged areas (E), then people displaced (A).
  2. Rescue efforts (D), then the forces and NGOs doing it (C). B-E-A-D-C.

Answer: option (3) — (B), (E), (A), (D), (C)

Q601CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q41NTA final key
Rearrange the jumbled phrases to make a meaningful sentence :
(A) having visited Europe
(B) nor French
(C) many times but he
(D) He boasts of
(E) can speak neither English
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (C), (D), (B), (E)
  2. (D), (A), (C), (E), (B)
  3. (E), (B), (C), (D), (E)
  4. (A), (D), (C), (E), (B)
Concept to recallCapital letter marks the start (He); neither precedes nor.
  1. ‘He boasts of (D) having visited Europe (A) many times but he (C) can speak neither English (E) nor French (B).’

Answer: option (2) — (D), (A), (C), (E), (B)

Q602CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q7NTA final key
Passage (summarised): building the Channel Tunnel

In 1984 France and Britain agreed that a link across the English Channel would benefit both and create jobs, but neither government could pay for so huge a project, so they held a contest. Entrants had to give a plan to raise the funds, be able to operate the link once built, and make it last at least 120 years.

Ten proposals came in, tunnels and bridges among them. Some were so “outlandish” they were easily dismissed; others too expensive ever to be finished. The winner planned two parallel railway tunnels under the Channel, with a third, smaller tunnel between them for maintenance (drainage pipes, communication cables and so on). After the first test run on 10 December 1993, the Channel Tunnel officially opened on 6 May 1994.

Arrange the following sentences in their order of occurrence in the passage.
(A) The successful proposal planned for a tunnel made up of two, parallel railway tunnels that would be dug.
(B) The proposed link must be able to endure for atleast 120 years.
(C) They decided to hold a contest
(D) A third smaller tunnel would be used for maintenance.
(E) Both the Governments realized that although the project would create the much needed jobs, neither could fund it.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B), (D), (C), (E)
  2. (E), (B), (C), (D), (A)
  3. (E), (C), (B), (A), (D)
  4. (C), (A), (B), (E), (D)
Concept to recallFollow cause → decision → rules → winner → detail of the winner.
  1. Problem of funding (E) leads to the contest (C).
  2. The contest’s rule of 120 years (B), then the winning design (A) and its third tunnel (D).
  3. E-C-B-A-D.

Answer: option (3) — (E), (C), (B), (A), (D)

Q603CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q20NTA final key
Rearrange the following sentences to make a meaningful paragraph:
(A) But there is one aspect of the James Web Space Telescope (TWIST) that is very limiting.
(B) To counter this limitations we can create Sky-survey telescope.
(C) It is designed to capture high-resolution images of small areas of the sky.
(D) The Vera Rubin observatory is being constructed specifically for this purpose.
(E) This is true for most telescope since it is difficult to create an image which is both wide and detailed.
  1. B, A, C, D, E
  2. C, A, B, D, E
  3. A, C, E, B, D
  4. D, C, B, A, E
Concept to recallPronoun and connector chain: ‘one aspect’ → ‘It is designed …’ → ‘This is true …’ → ‘To counter this …’ → ‘for this purpose’.
  1. A introduces the limitation; C explains it (only small areas in high resolution).
  2. E generalises (‘This is true for most telescopes’); B gives the remedy (sky-survey telescopes).
  3. D names one built ‘for this purpose’. A-C-E-B-D.

Answer: option (3) — A, C, E, B, D

Q604CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q21NTA final key
Rearrange the following sentences to form a paragraph:
(A) But there is no denying that the discovery of geological time helped people come to terms with the idea that living things have had plenty of time to change.
(B) The key evidence for evolution comes from living organisms.
(C) British scientist began to consider geological time during the 18th century.
(D) Even if fossils and rocks did not exist we would still conclude that evolution occurs.
  1. C, A, D, B
  2. D, B, A, C
  3. B, D, A, C
  4. B, D, C, A
Concept to recallTopic sentence first (B states the main claim); ‘Even if …’ (D) supports it; ‘But there is no denying …’ (A) concedes a point; C gives the history behind that concession.
  1. B: the key evidence for evolution comes from living organisms.
  2. D: even without fossils and rocks we would still conclude evolution occurs.
  3. A: But geological time did help people accept that living things had time to change.
  4. C: British scientists began considering geological time in the 18th century. B-D-A-C.

Answer: option (3) — B, D, A, C

TrapC looks like an opener because it gives a date, but A’s ‘But’ must answer D, not C.
Q605CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q42NTA final key
Rearrange the following phrases to make a meaningful sentence:
(A) swung the hammer
(B) and banged my thumb
(C) when I
(D) without aiming properly
(E) I missed the nail
  1. E, D, C, A, B
  2. C, A, D, E, B
  3. A, B, C, E, D
  4. D, C, A, E, B
Concept to recallTime clause first: ‘When I …, I …’.
  1. ‘When I (C) swung the hammer (A) without aiming properly (D), I missed the nail (E) and banged my thumb (B).’

Answer: option (2) — C, A, D, E, B

Q606CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q8NTA final key
Passage (summarised): Arjun and the rasgullas

Arjun’s mother brings home his favourite thing, an earthen pot of rasgullas, keeps it in the refrigerator and gives him the biggest of the “shining, rotund figures”, telling him to eat slowly instead of gulping.

He skips his daytime nap, sneaks out of his mother’s room while everyone sleeps — his mind “the devil’s workshop” — and searches the fridge for the “prized item”. Unable to find the “soft and syrupy sponges”, he moves things about, slams the door and leaves, making a mess and leaving the tap running.

That evening his “livid” father drags him into the drawing room; Arjun “feigned” weeping, his grandparents snatch him away from his father, and he breaks free, throws himself on the bed and pretends to sleep. At dinner he refuses food while everyone tries to “coax” him; when his grandfather asks what would make him feel better, he says, “Rasgulla! Give me at least ten.”

Arrange the following activities performed by Arjun in a chronological sequence:
(A) Asking for Rasgulla
(B) Searching for Rasgulla
(C) Falling on his bed
(D) Sneaking out of his mother’s room
(E) Eating the Rasgulla
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. B, A, E, D, C
  2. C, D, B, A, E
  3. E, D, B, C, A
  4. A, B, C, D, E
Concept to recallTrace the story: first rasgulla, the raid, the punishment, the dinner demand.
  1. He eats the one his mother gives him (E), sneaks out (D), searches the fridge (B).
  2. After the scolding he throws himself on the bed (C), and at dinner asks for ten (A). E-D-B-C-A.

Answer: option (3) — E, D, B, C, A

Q607CUET 2022 · 16 Sep, Shift 1 · Set 42 · Q23key re-derived
Rearrange the given groups of words to make a meaningful sentence:
(A) a consumer protection drive to educate
(B) against using fraudulent means
(C) the people about their rights and to warn traders
(D) the administration will soon launch
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. D, A, C, B
  2. B, C, A, D
  3. C, A, B, D
  4. D, C, B, A
Concept to recallSentence rearrangement: find the part with the subject + main verb to open, then join parts by grammar (an unfinished phrase such as on the or may be needs its completion next).
  1. (D) has subject and verb: The administration will soon launch — launch what? (A) a consumer protection drive to educate.
  2. Educate whom? (C) the people about their rights and to warn traders; warn them (B) against using fraudulent means.

Answer: option (1) — D, A, C, B

Q608CUET 2022 · 16 Sep, Shift 1 · Set 42 · Q24worked here
Rearrange the given groups of words to make a meaningful sentence:
(A) no part of this publication may be
(B) in any form without the written permission
(C) of the publisher of the book
(D) reproduced, stored or transmitted
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. B, A, C, D
  2. B, D, A, C
  3. A, D, B ,C
  4. C, D, A, B
Concept to recallSentence rearrangement: find the part with the subject + main verb to open, then join parts by grammar (an unfinished phrase such as on the or may be needs its completion next).
  1. (A) holds the subject: No part of this publication may be … and may be needs a past participle: (D) reproduced, stored or transmitted.
  2. Then (B) in any form without the written permission and (C) of the publisher of the book.
  3. This is the copyright line printed in most books: A, D, B, C.

Answer: option (3) — A, D, B ,C

NoteCollegedunia’s typed solution gives B, D, A, C; that is wrong for the reason above. Starting with (B) leaves no subject before the verb.
Q609CUET 2022 · 16 Sep, Shift 1 · Set 42 · Q25key re-derived
Rearrange the given groups of words to make a meaningful sentence:
(A) then the world will avert all future wars
(B) and agree to obey all the laws
(C) if all the nations work together
(D) for the common good of mankind
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. D, B, A, C
  2. B, C, A, D
  3. C, D, B, A
  4. A, D, B, C
Concept to recallSentence rearrangement: find the part with the subject + main verb to open, then join parts by grammar (an unfinished phrase such as on the or may be needs its completion next). An if … then sentence puts the condition first and the then-clause last.
  1. The if-clause (C) opens; (D) for the common good of mankind completes “work together”.
  2. (B) and agree to obey all the laws adds a second condition; (A) then the world will avert… is the result.

Answer: option (3) — C, D, B, A

Q610CUET 2022 · 16 Sep, Shift 1 · Set 42 · Q26worked here
Rearrange the given groups of words to make a meaningful sentence:
(A) for the vehicles carrying food items
(B) the Centre has made it mandatory
(C) to display all details on the
(D) windshield and the rear screen
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. D, C, B, A
  2. C, B, D, A
  3. A, C, D, A,
  4. B, A, C, D
Concept to recallSentence rearrangement: find the part with the subject + main verb to open, then join parts by grammar (an unfinished phrase such as on the or may be needs its completion next). made it mandatory for X to do Y is the fixed pattern.
  1. (B) The Centre has made it mandatory opens; mandatory for whom? (A) for the vehicles carrying food items.
  2. To do what? (C) to display all details on the … (D) windshield and the rear screen.
  3. B, A, C, D is the only printed option that keeps on the directly before its object.

Answer: option (4) — B, A, C, D

NoteCollegedunia gives B, C, D, A, which is not one of the printed options (and would strand for the vehicles… at the end).

Error Spotting and Sentence Correction38 questions

Q611CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q21NTA final key
Choose the option which is grammatically correct:
  1. She is enough wise to decide on the right course of action.
  2. She is wise enough to decide on the right course of action.
  3. She is too wise to decide on the right course of action.
  4. She is wise rather to decide on the right course of action.
Concept to recallEnough follows an adjective: “wise enough to”. Too … to has a negative sense.
  1. “enough wise” is the wrong order.
  2. “too wise to decide” would mean she cannot decide because she is wise – absurd.
  3. “wise rather to” is ungrammatical. ⇒ option 2.

Answer: option (2) — She is wise enough to decide on the right course of action.

Q612CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q38NTA final key
Given below are four sentences.Choose the one which is grammatically correct:-
  1. I gave him a few coins I had.
  2. I gave him few coins I had.
  3. I gave him the few coins I had.
  4. I gave him the fewer coins I had.
Concept to recalla few = some; few = hardly any; the few = all of the small number (specific, defined by “I had”).
  1. The coins are specified (“I had”) – all the small number ⇒ the few.
  2. “a few … I had” and “few … I had” lack the definite article; “the fewer” is a wrong comparative.

Answer: option (3) — I gave him the few coins I had.

Q613CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q31NTA final key
Which of the following statements is incorrect?
  1. The lion and the unicorn fought for the crown.
  2. Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall.
  3. Here is the watch that you asked for.
  4. There is a cattle into the field,
Concept to recallcattle is a plural noun (no singular form, never “a cattle”): The cattle are in the field.
  1. “a cattle” is wrong (cattle is plural), and into (motion) should be in (position).
  2. The other three are correct sentences.

Answer: option (4) — There is a cattle into the field,

Q614CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q31NTA final key
Choose the sentences with the correct use of prepositions in the following options.
(A) A few of the glaciers are expected to vanish by 2050.
(B) They never turned up their proposal.
(C) It was the last report filed by the company in last month.
(D) I am indebted for you regarding help.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A) and (B) Only
  2. (A) Only
  3. (B) and (C) Only
  4. (B) and (D) Only
Concept to recallby + a date = not later than; turn down = reject (turn up = arrive/appear); no preposition before last month; indebted to a person for a thing.
  1. (A) is correct.
  2. (B) should be turned down; (C) drop in; (D) should be indebted to you for your help.

Answer: option (2) — (A) Only

NoteCollegedunia gives (A) and (B); NTA’s key gives (A) only.
Q615CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q36NTA final key
Choose the correct version of the given sentence from the options below :
The committee told me that they have already been processed the file.
  1. The committee told me that they has already processed the file.
  2. The committee told me that they had already processed the file.
  3. The committee told me that they had been processed the file.
  4. The committee told me that they have process the file.
Concept to recallReported speech after a past reporting verb: present perfect → past perfect (had + V3); and active voice since the committee did the processing.
  1. After told, have processed becomes had processed; been must go (it makes a wrong passive).
  2. they has breaks agreement; have process lacks the participle.

Answer: option (2) — The committee told me that they had already processed the file.

Q616CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q36NTA final key
Choose the part of the sentence which has an error -
(A) The Japanese
(B) become very exciting
(C) about new fashion ideas
(D) but the trends only last a short while
(E) No error
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A) Only
  2. (B) Only
  3. (C) Only
  4. (D) Only
Concept to recall-ed adjectives describe how a person feels (excited); -ing adjectives describe what causes the feeling (exciting).
  1. People feel excitement about ideas → ‘become very excited about’.

Answer: option (2) — (B) Only

Q617CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q37NTA final key
Pick the incorrect part in the given sentence.
The blessings that the habit of reading confers/on their possessor/are many provided we/choose the right kind of books.
  1. The blessings that the habit of reading confers
  2. on their possessor
  3. are many provided we
  4. choose the right kind of books
Concept to recallA pronoun agrees with its antecedent in number.
  1. The possessor is the possessor of the habit (singular) → ‘on its possessor’.

Answer: option (2) — on their possessor

Trap‘blessings’ is plural, but it is the habit, not the blessings, that has a possessor.
Q618CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q36NTA final key
Choose the part of the sentence that has an error:
  1. No sooner she had realized
  2. her blunder than
  3. she began
  4. to take corrective measures
Concept to recallNo sooner at the head of a clause takes inversion: No sooner had she realized … than …
  1. ‘No sooner she had’ → ‘No sooner had she’.

Answer: option (1) — No sooner she had realized

Q619CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q37NTA final key
Choose the part of a sentence that is grammatically incorrect
  1. What has excited many
  2. in India is how AI can be a
  3. powerful change agent by
  4. bridge the digital divide
Concept to recallA preposition is followed by a noun or gerund, not a bare verb.
  1. ‘by bridge’ → ‘by bridging the digital divide’.

Answer: option (4) — bridge the digital divide

Q620CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 3 · Q18NTA final key
Choose the part of the following sentence that contains an error :
Ranjeeta does not usually prefer staying at cottages, but last winter she spent few days in one.
  1. Ranjeeta does not usually
  2. prefer staying at cottages
  3. But last winters
  4. She spent few days into one
Concept to recalla few = some (positive); few = hardly any (negative). Static location takes in, not into.
  1. She spent a few days in one.

Answer: option (4) — She spent few days into one

NoteNTA’s final key accepts both (3) and (4): option (3) is printed ‘last winters’, which is itself an error (and does not match the sentence), while (4) carries the intended errors few and into.
Q621CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 3 · Q19NTA final key
Choose the part of the following sentence that contains an error :
The most important feature of our products are that they are all created by hand.
  1. The most important feature
  2. of our products are that
  3. they are all
  4. created by hand
Concept to recallThe verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, not with a noun inside an of-phrase.
  1. Head noun = feature (singular) → ‘of our products is that’.

Answer: option (2) — of our products are that

Q622CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 3 · Q36NTA final key
Choose the part of the following sentence that contains an error :
If a company sends its employees abroad to work for a foreign client, they pays them a daily allowance.
  1. If a company
  2. Sends its employees abroad
  3. To work for a foreign client, they
  4. Pays them a daily allowance
Concept to recallPronoun and verb must agree with the antecedent: a company → it pays.
  1. The subject should be ‘it pays’; NTA marks the part with the verb, ‘pays them a daily allowance’.

Answer: option (4) — Pays them a daily allowance

NoteThe faulty word ‘they’ sits at the end of part (3), so (3) is arguable too; NTA’s final key is (4).
Q623CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 3 · Q37NTA final key
Choose the part of the following sentence that contains an error :
It is the quarter to ten by my watch.
  1. It is the
  2. quarter to ten
  3. by my watch
  4. No error
Concept to recallClock time: a quarter to/past (indefinite article).
  1. ‘It is a quarter to ten’.

Answer: option (1) — It is the

Q624CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 1 · Q18NTA final key
Spot the error in the following sentence
  1. It is often said that
  2. some men are born great
  3. some achieve greatness and
  4. some had greatness threst on them
Concept to recallKeep tenses parallel in a list of general truths; the idiom (from Twelfth Night) is “some have greatness thrust upon them”.
  1. The first two clauses are in the present (are born, achieve), so the third must be have, not past had.
  2. The verb is also misspelt: thrust, not threst.

Answer: option (4) — some had greatness threst on them

Q625CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 1 · Q36NTA final key
The given sentence is divided into three parts. Scan it carefully for errors and choose the most appropriate options
A) I found less | B) books in the| C) library than that
  1. A only
  2. B and C
  3. C only
  4. No error
Concept to recallfewer + countable plural (fewer books); less + uncountable (less water).
  1. books are countable, so part A should read I found fewer.
  2. Parts B and C are as printed in the source (the comparison is left incomplete there).

Answer: option (1) — A only

Q626CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 1 · Q37NTA final key
The given sentence is divided into tissue parts. scan it carefully for errors and choose the most appropriate options
A) Few persons
B) are free
C) from worries
  1. A only
  2. A and C
  3. C only
  4. No errors
Concept to recallpeople is the usual plural of person; persons is formal/legal (“persons authorised”).
  1. NTA marks part A: in a general statement the natural plural is Few people.
  2. are free from worries is correct: free from is the right preposition and are agrees with a plural subject.

Answer: option (1) — A only

NoteFew persons are free from worries is not strictly ungrammatical, so “No errors” is arguable; NTA’s final key gives (1) A only.
Q627CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 1 · Q40NTA final key
Which of the following sentences demonstrate appropriate use(s) of asterisks
  1. The third and fourth chapter will be tested in exam
  2. The third and fourth chapters will be tested in the exam
  3. Third and fourth chapter will be tested in the exam
  4. The third and fourth chapters will be tested in the exam [printed identical to (2)]
Concept to recallTwo ordinals before one noun (the third and fourth) refer to two things, so the noun is plural; a particular exam takes the.
  1. (“asterisks” is a misprint for articles.)
  2. (1) and (3) keep chapter singular and drop an article.
  3. (2) and (4) are printed identically and both are correct; NTA keys (2).

Answer: option (2) — The third and fourth chapters will be tested in the exam

NoteOptions (2) and (4) are word-for-word the same in the paper. NTA’s final key gives (2).
Q628CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 1 · Q42NTA final key
Read the following sentence care. Some part of the sentence may have an error. Choose the most appropriate options.
Mumbai (A) | is New York (B) | of India (c)
  1. A
  2. B
  3. C
  4. No error
Concept to recallA proper noun used as a common noun (as a type) takes the: the New York of India, the Shakespeare of India.
  1. Mumbai is being called a city like New York → is the New York (part B).

Answer: option (2) — B

Q629CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q36NTA final key
Identify the error in the following sentence.
Each girl and each boy was given a red pencil.
  1. Each girl and each boy
  2. was given
  3. a red pencil
  4. No error
Concept to recallTwo singular subjects each preceded by each or every take a singular verb.
  1. Each girl and each boy → singular was given is correct; no error.

Answer: option (4) — No error

Q630CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q37NTA final key
Identify the error in the following sentence.
He was not able to concentrate because of the continual music being played next door.
  1. He was not able to concentrate
  2. because of the continual music
  3. being played next door
  4. No error
Concept to recallcontinuous = without a break; continual = repeated with interruptions.
  1. Music playing without a pause is continuous music; so the error is in part 2.

Answer: option (2) — because of the continual music

Q631CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q47NTA final key
Some part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect. Pick the error.
Another surprising change that I noticed in him in recent times is that he avoids to speak to me.
  1. Another surprising change
  2. that is noticed in him in recent time
  3. is that he avoids
  4. to speak to me
Concept to recallavoid takes a gerund, never an infinitive: avoid speaking.
  1. he avoids to speak → he avoids speaking to me; the error is in part 4.

Answer: option (4) — to speak to me

Q632CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q26NTA final key
Choose the sentence that does not have the articles placed correctly :
  1. This is a same pen that I borrowed from you last week.
  2. Maya is most likely the person to lead us.
  3. I will not be having breakfast today.
  4. Suyesh will be moving to a European city next month.
Concept to recallsame always takes the: the same pen. a European (sound /j/), an hour (vowel sound).
  1. (1) a same pen → the same pen.
  2. (4) is correct: European begins with a /j/ sound, so a.

Answer: option (1) — This is a same pen that I borrowed from you last week.

Trap(4) tempts students who think every vowel letter takes an.
NoteNTA’s provisional key gave (2); the final key of 12 Jul 2023 (and the Feb 2024 revised file) corrected it to (1), which is plainly right.
Q633CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q36worked here
Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error :
  1. scarcely did I reach the station
  2. nervous and tense than the train sped away
  3. leaving me lonely in a strange place
  4. No error
Concept to recallScarcely / Hardly … when; No sooner … than. Mixing them is the classic error.
  1. Scarcely must be followed by when, so than in segment 2 is wrong.
  2. Segment 1 is also faulty: after Scarcely the past perfect is needed — Scarcely had I reached the station … when the train sped away. With two faulty segments and only one to choose, NTA dropped the item; segment 2 holds the classic error.

Answer: option (2) — nervous and tense than the train sped away

NoteNTA dropped this question in the final key, so every candidate was given the marks. The answer shown is our own reading.
Q634CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q37NTA final key
Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error :
  1. your short story should feature a protagonist
  2. who undergoes a challenging situation
  3. which result in new learning
  4. as self discovery of some kind
Concept to recallA relative pronoun takes the number of its antecedent.
  1. which refers to a challenging situation (singular) → which results.

Answer: option (3) — which result in new learning

Q635CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q36NTA final key
Spot the error in the following sentence and choose the appropriate option.
Children gained security from knowing exactly where their parents draw the line.
  1. draw
  2. gained
  3. knowing
  4. from
Concept to recallSequence of tenses: a general truth stated in the present (‘draw’) needs a present main verb (‘gain’).
  1. The sentence states a general truth about children; ‘draw’ is present.
  2. So ‘gained’ should be ‘gain’.

Answer: option (2) — gained

Q636CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q37NTA final key
Spot the error in the following sentence and choose the appropriate option.
Democracy is the system in which people could exercise some control over their rulers.
  1. is
  2. could
  3. exercise
  4. over
Concept to recallKeep tenses consistent: a definition in the present (‘Democracy is’) needs can, not could.
  1. ‘Democracy is the system in which people can exercise …’
  2. ‘control over’ is correct.

Answer: option (2) — could

Q637CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 2 · Q36NTA final key
Spot the error in the given part of the sentence.
If there is no error, mark that part as your answer.
(A) If you do not
(B) Know the meaning
(C) of any word,
(D) Please see in the dictionary
(E) No error
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) only
  2. (D) only
  3. (B) and (C) only
  4. (E) only
Concept to recallPhrasal verb: look up a word in a dictionary, or consult a dictionary; ‘see in’ is unidiomatic.
  1. (A)–(C) form a correct conditional clause.
  2. (D) should read ‘please look it up in the dictionary’ / ‘consult the dictionary’.

Answer: option (2) — (D) only

Q638CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 2 · Q37NTA final key
Spot the error in the following sentence.
If there is no error choose the appropriate option.
I never remember having met a more interesting man in my life.
  1. I never remember
  2. having met a more
  3. interesting man in my life
  4. No error
Concept to recallremember refers to the present state of memory: ‘I don’t remember ever having met …’; ‘never remember’ means habitually forgetting.
  1. The sense intended is ‘I do not remember ever having met …’.
  2. So the error is in the first part, ‘I never remember’.

Answer: option (1) — I never remember

Q639CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 2 · Q47NTA final key
Choose the grammatically correct omitted part of the sentence from the following list :
  1. It is a tale
  2. told by idiot
  3. full of sound and fury
  4. signifying nothing
Concept to recallThe line is Macbeth’s ‘It is a tale / told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, / signifying nothing’: a singular countable noun needs an article.
  1. Each part is correct except ‘told by idiot’, which has lost the article an.
  2. The (confusingly worded) question wants the part from which a word was omitted: option (2).

Answer: option (2) — told by idiot

NoteThe stem is garbled as printed; NTA’s key (2) shows it means ‘the part with the omission’.
Q640CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q30NTA final key
Choose the correct alternative from the options for the underlined words. In case your response is ‘No Improvement’ mark that as your answer.
Children should be taught to write by a fountain pen.
  1. No Improvement
  2. Through
  3. with
  4. from
Concept to recallInstrument used = with (write with a pen); by is for means/agent (by hand, by post).
  1. A pen is an instrument → ‘write with a fountain pen’.

Answer: option (3) — with

Q641CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q31NTA final key
Choose the appropriate alternative for the underlined word.
You should at least congratulate your friend for his grand success in the elections.
  1. at
  2. on
  3. upon
  4. to
Concept to recallCongratulate someone on something.
  1. Standard: ‘congratulate him on his success’.
  2. ‘congratulate for’ is a common error; ‘upon’ is old-fashioned and not keyed.

Answer: option (2) — on

Q642CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q36NTA final key
Spot the error in the given parts of a sentence. In case of no error, mark that option as your answer.
(A) This girl wrote the essay
(B) So well
(C) that her teacher was exceedingly
(D) pleased with it.
(E) No error
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (C) Only
  2. (A) and (B) Only
  3. (E) Only
  4. (D) Only
Concept to recallso … that is a correct correlative; pleased with is the right preposition.
  1. ‘wrote the essay so well that her teacher was exceedingly pleased with it’ is correct throughout.
  2. So: no error.

Answer: option (3) — (E) Only

Q643CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q37NTA final key
Spot the error in the given parts of a sentence.
In case of no error, mark that option as your answer.
(A) Magic realism is one
(B) of the latest
(C) addition to good literature
(D) published to good recent tunes
(E) No error
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (B) Only
  2. (C) and (D) Only
  3. (C) Only
  4. (E) Only
Concept to recall‘one of the …’ is followed by a plural noun; and every part must make sense with the rest.
  1. (C): ‘one of the latest additions’ — addition must be plural.
  2. (D): ‘published to good recent tunes’ makes no sense after ‘literature’ (a genre is not ‘published to tunes’); it is also faulty.
  3. So (C) and (D).

Answer: option (2) — (C) and (D) Only

Trap(3) catches only the grammatical slip and misses the nonsensical last part.
Q644CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q47NTA final key
Choose the grammatically correct form of the sentence below from the options given.
My uncle is enough rich to buy a car.
  1. My uncle is rich enough to buy a car.
  2. My uncle is richer enough to buy a car.
  3. My uncle in enough richer to buy a car.
  4. No error
Concept to recallenough comes after an adjective or adverb (rich enough) but before a noun (enough money).
  1. ‘rich enough to buy’.
  2. A comparative (richer) cannot take enough.

Answer: option (1) — My uncle is rich enough to buy a car.

Q645CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q36NTA final key
Select the incorrect sentences from the following options:
(A) The roof collapsed that very moment.
(B) This is more than flesh and blood can endure.
(C) He puts on an air of dignity.
(D) The tailor’s bill has hurried up to a large amount.
(E) They were very grateful to him for kindness.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, E only
  2. A, D, E only
  3. A, B, D, E only
  4. C, D, E only
Concept to recallCheck prepositions, phrasal verbs and determiners one sentence at a time.
  1. A needs at: ‘at that very moment’.
  2. D: a bill runs up (mounts up) to a sum, it does not ‘hurry up’.
  3. E needs a possessive: ‘for his kindness’.
  4. B (an idiom) and C (‘puts on an air of’) are correct. So A, D, E.

Answer: option (2) — A, D, E only

Q646CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q37NTA final key
Select the incorrect sentences from the following options:
(A) We discussed about the matter yesterday.
(B) It is not likely that he will see his home again.
(C) I would rather you went through air.
(D) The negotiations were rattled off in secret.
(E) He urged them to be quiet and listen to his words.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. C, D, E only
  2. A, B, C only
  3. A, C, D only
  4. A and D only
Concept to recalldiscuss takes a direct object (no ‘about’); travel by air; negotiations are carried on, while ‘rattle off’ = recite quickly.
  1. A: ‘discussed the matter’.
  2. C: ‘went by air’ (‘would rather you went’ itself is correct).
  3. D: ‘rattled off’ is the wrong phrasal verb (carried on / conducted).
  4. B and E are correct. So A, C, D.

Answer: option (3) — A, C, D only

Q647CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q45NTA final key
Which of the following sentences demonstrate an incorrect form of the adverb?
(A) The moon shine bright in the day.
(B) You are pretty mistaken about him.
(C) He never comes late.
(D) It would hardly rain today.
(E) The have ran more faster than the dog.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A and E only
  2. A and C only
  3. B and C only
  4. D and E only
Concept to recallA verb is modified by an adverb (shine brightly); no double comparative (more faster).
  1. A: ‘bright’ used where an adverb is wanted (and the sun, not the moon, shines by day).
  2. E: ‘more faster’ is a double comparative; ‘much faster’ is right.
  3. B (pretty = rather), C and D are acceptable. So A and E.

Answer: option (1) — A and E only

Q648CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q47NTA final key
The following sentence is grammatically incorrect:
A great person use to lived in this house.
Correct the sentence above by choosing the most appropriate option:
  1. A great person lived to use in that house.
  2. A great person used to lived in that house.
  3. A great person used to live in this house.
  4. A great person use to lived in that house.
Concept to recallused to + base verb for past habits or states.
  1. ‘used to live’: past form used, then the bare infinitive live.
  2. (2) and (4) keep ‘lived’; (1) changes the meaning.

Answer: option (3) — A great person used to live in this house.

Fill in the Blanks and Cloze78 questions

Q649CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q22NTA final key
Fill in the blanks with the most suitable word from the options given below:
The desire for revenge is very dangerous _____ it does not diminish with time.
  1. whereas
  2. while
  3. because
  4. so
Concept to recallChoose the conjunction by the logical relation: the second clause gives the reason.
  1. Why is it dangerous? It does not diminish with time ⇒ because.
  2. Whereas/while show contrast; so shows result (it would reverse the logic).

Answer: option (3) — because

Q650CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q23NTA final key
Select the appropriate word to fill in the blank:
Rahul thought he had a good chance to get the job _____ his uncle was on the company's board of directors.
  1. but
  2. yet
  3. since
  4. unless
Concept to recallSince = because (reason).
  1. His uncle on the board is the reason for his hope ⇒ since.
  2. But/yet = contrast; unless = condition (if not).

Answer: option (3) — since

Q651CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q33NTA final key
Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate option :
Kindness is a quality that is alien _____ Harish.
  1. for
  2. to
  3. about
  4. of
Concept to recallFixed preposition: alien to = foreign to, not part of someone’s nature.
  1. alien to someone.

Answer: option (2) — to

Q652CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q34NTA final key
Fill in the blanks with the most suitable option :
The two brothers quarrelled _____ the share of their ancestral property.
  1. for
  2. at
  3. over
  4. off
Concept to recallQuarrel with a person, over/about a thing.
  1. The subject of the dispute is a thing ⇒ quarrelled over.
  2. “for, at, off” do not collocate.

Answer: option (3) — over

Q653CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q16NTA final key
Fill in the blanks given in List-I with the correct words given in List-II
List IList II
(A) He has changed a lot _________ I last saw him.(I) although
(B) She arrived on time______ it was raining cats and dogs.(II) unless
(C) ________ there is an emergency don't disturb me.(III) as
(D) Do unto others______ you would have them do unto you.(IV) since

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (I), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (III)
  3. (A) - (IV), (B) - (I), (C) - (II), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)
Concept to recallsince (from a time, with present perfect); although (concession); unless (= if not); as (in the same way that).
  1. “has changed … I last saw him” ⇒ since (A-IV).
  2. On time despite rain ⇒ although (B-I).
  3. Do not disturb if there is no emergency ⇒ unless (C-II).
  4. Do unto others as … (the Golden Rule) ⇒ as (D-III).

Answer: option (3) — (A) - (IV), (B) - (I), (C) - (II), (D) - (III)

Q654CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q32NTA final key
Fill in the blank by selecting the appropriate word from the options given below:-
As Rohit was driving fast, his car hit  the divider and fell ------------ a ditch.
  1. on
  2. into
  3. inside
  4. under
Concept to recallInto shows movement from outside to inside; in/inside show position.
  1. The car moved and ended up in the ditch ⇒ fell into.
  2. “inside” describes position, not motion; “on/under” do not fit a ditch.

Answer: option (2) — into

Q655CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q37NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the appropriate word from the options given below.-
It is really difficult to deal ___those people who do not want to listen to others .
  1. at
  2. about
  3. after
  4. with
Concept to recallDeal with (people or a problem) = handle, cope with.
  1. deal with people.

Answer: option (4) — with

Q656CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q39NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the appropriate word from the options given below:
The director is a perfectionist,_____, he is seldom satisfied with average performance
  1. hence
  2. however
  3. nevertheless
  4. but
Concept to recallLinkers: hence (result); however / nevertheless / but (contrast).
  1. Being a perfectionist causes dissatisfaction with average work ⇒ result ⇒ hence.
  2. The other three signal a contrast that is not there.

Answer: option (1) — hence

Q657CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q6NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the appropriate word from the options given:
As an employee working for a long time, you know too _______ who could have spilled the beans.
  1. more
  2. little
  3. few
  4. well
Concept to recallFixed expression: know (only) too well = know very well, often regretfully.
  1. “You know too well who…” = you know perfectly who leaked the secret.
  2. “too little” contradicts “working for a long time”; “too more/too few” are ungrammatical here.

Answer: option (4) — well

Q658CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q24NTA final key
Fill in the blanks in the sentences given in List – I with the appropriate phrasal verbs given in List -II:-
List IList II
(A) Despite searching for hours, she couldn't find her keys, but they eventually____ in her jacket(I) turn down
(B) The old factory was eventually ___ a vibrant art gallery, preserving its historical significance.(II) turn on
(C) Before leaving the room, she remembered to____ the air conditioner to keep it cool.(III) turned up
(D) She had to ___ the volume of the music to avoid disturbing her neighbours late at night.(IV) turned into

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)
  3. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)
Concept to recallTurn up = be found / appear; turn into = become; turn on = switch on; turn down = lower (volume).
  1. Keys “turned up” (were found) → III.
  2. Factory “turned into” a gallery → IV.
  3. “turn on” the AC to keep it cool → II; “turn down” the volume → I.

Answer: option (4) — (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)

Trap“Turn up” also means raise volume, which would make the neighbours angrier – read sentence D to the end.
Q659CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q28NTA final key
Fill in the blanks in the sentences given in List-I with the appropriate words given in List-II :-
List IList II
(A) Ika Jena is an Odia food ________who documents and showcases Odia cuisine on her blog Culinary Xpress.(I) chef
(B) Gitika Saikia identifies herself as an Assamese food _______ who specialises in tribal and mainland Assamese cuisines.(II) entrepreneur

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (III), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (II)
  3. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)
Concept to recallChronicler = one who records/documents; repertoire = a stock or range of items; entrepreneur = one who runs a business.

  2. C needs a noun for a collection of breads ⇒ repertoire (C-IV).
  3. “specialises in … cuisines” ⇒ chef (B-I); D “culinary entrepreneur” (D-II).

Q660CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q29NTA final key
Fill in the blanks in the given sentences of List-I with the appropriate words given in List-II:-
List IList II
(A) I read the mystery novels ___ they captivate my imagination.(I) Unless
(B) This is the place _____ he was born.(II) because
(C) Many things have happened ___ we met last time.(III) Where
(D) _____ you tell me the truth, I will not allow you to go.(IV) Since

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  2. (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I)
  3. (A) - (III), (B) - (I), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV)
  4. (A) - (IV), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (I)
Concept to recallConjunctions: because (reason), where (place), since (point of time with present perfect), unless (= if not).
  1. Reason ⇒ because (A-II); place ⇒ where (B-III).
  2. “have happened … we met” ⇒ since (C-IV).
  3. “___ you tell me the truth, I will not allow” ⇒ unless (D-I).

Q661CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q33NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct word from the options given below to make a meaningful sentence:-
Ten tourists were _____ injured in the accident and a few of them succumbed to their injuries on the way to the hospital.
  1. spuriously
  2. gravely
  3. fatefully
  4. vitally
Concept to recallCollocation: gravely / seriously / critically injured.
  1. Some later died ⇒ the injuries were serious ⇒ gravely.
  2. Spuriously = falsely; fatefully = with momentous results; vitally = essentially – none collocates with “injured”.

Answer: option (2) — gravely

Trap“Fatefully” sounds right because some died, but it does not describe the degree of injury.
Q662CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q34NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct word from the options given below to make a meaningful sentence:-
In my haste to stop the boiling milk from overflowing, I accidentally _______ my fingers.
  1. sizzled
  2. scorched
  3. scalded
  4. sunburnt
Concept to recallScald = burn with hot liquid or steam; scorch = burn the surface with dry heat.
  1. Boiling milk is a hot liquid ⇒ scalded.
  2. Sizzle is the sound of frying; sunburnt needs the sun; scorch is dry heat.

Answer: option (3) — scalded

Trap“Scorched” is the near-miss; it is for dry heat (an iron scorches a shirt).
Q663CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q35NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct word from the options given below to make a meaningful sentence:-
His salary is in ________ with the amount of work he does.
  1. accord
  2. coordination
  3. balance
  4. keeping
Concept to recallFixed phrase in keeping with = consistent with, appropriate to.
  1. “in ___ with” ⇒ in keeping with.
  2. In accord with exists but means “in agreement with” (opinions, rules), not in proportion; NTA keys “keeping”.
  3. “in coordination with” is for joint action; “in balance with” is not idiomatic here.

Answer: option (4) — keeping

Trap“accord” is the close distractor.
Q664CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q37NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct word from the options given below:-
She is standing____her husband in this crisis.
  1. with
  2. in
  3. for
  4. by
Concept to recallPhrasal verb stand by someone = support them loyally, especially in difficulty.
  1. Support in a crisis ⇒ stand by.
  2. “Stand with” (show solidarity) is modern usage but not the idiom tested; “stand for” = represent/tolerate; “stand in” = substitute (needs “for”).

Answer: option (4) — by

Trap“with” sounds natural; the set idiom for loyal support is “stand by”.
Q665CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q38NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct option:-
The two friends appear to have fallen _________ over a minor issue.
  1. down
  2. out
  3. into
  4. by
Concept to recallFall out (with someone) = quarrel.
  1. Friends + “over a minor issue” ⇒ quarrelled ⇒ fallen out.
  2. Fall down = drop; fall into = enter; fall by (the wayside) = fail.

Answer: option (2) — out

Q666CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q39NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct option:-
The committee’s appeal to the people for money _________ little response.
  1. evoked
  2. provided
  3. provoked
  4. prevented
Concept to recallEvoke a response = call forth; provoke = stir up, usually anger.
  1. An appeal draws out (or fails to draw out) a response ⇒ evoked little response.
  2. “Provoked” implies an angry reaction; “provided/prevented” do not fit the sense.

Answer: option (1) — evoked

TrapEvoke vs provoke: both take “response”, but provoke suggests irritation.
Q667CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q11NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
The President finally had to ____________ the demands of the public for his resignation.
  1. ignore
  2. initiate
  3. accede to
  4. condone
Concept to recallaccede to = agree to a demand or request (often reluctantly).
  1. finally had to signals giving in → accede to the demands.
  2. ignore contradicts finally had to; you cannot initiate someone else’s demands; condone = overlook a wrong, which does not fit demands.

Answer: option (3) — accede to

Q668CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q2NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
The candidate assured the interviewers that the dip in her grades during her second semester was an ___________ since she had always been a top scorer in the first semester.
  1. anomaly
  2. allay
  3. adage
  4. abatement
Concept to recallanomaly = something that deviates from what is normal or expected.
  1. A single low semester in a record of top scores is an exception to the pattern → anomaly.

Answer: option (1) — anomaly

Q669CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q4NTA final key

Q671CUET 2024 · 29 May (Delhi re-scheduled) · Code A · Q22NTA final key

Q679CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q26NTA final key
Match the blanks in List I with suitable Articles in List II
List-IList-II
(A) ______ unreasonably long explanation was given by the defaulter.(I) No article

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

  2. A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II
  3. A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
  4. A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
Concept to recallArticles: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound (an hour, an MP; a university, a European, a one-year-old); the for a specific/known thing or a unique name (the BBC); no article before plural nouns used generally.
  1. unreasonably begins with a vowel sound → an (A-III).
  2. The BBC: a named organisation read as letters takes the (B-IV).
  3. universal begins with a “yoo” (consonant) sound → a (C-II).

Q680CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q27NTA final key

  3. a

Concept to recallArticles: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound (an hour, an MP; a university, a European, a one-year-old); the for a specific/known thing or a unique name (the BBC); no article before plural nouns used generally.

Q682CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q32NTA final key

  4. a the
Concept to recallthe + adjective names a whole class of people: the rich, the poor, the bold and the beautiful.
  1. ‘the bold and the beautiful’ = bold and beautiful people as a class.
  2. Both blanks take the.

Answer: option (2) — the, The

Q717CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q27NTA final key
Fill in the blanks with suitable Articles.
January is _________ first month of _________ year.
Choose the appropriate option :
  1. a, an
  2. The, an
  3. A, The
  4. The The
Concept to recallOrdinals (first, second) take the; a unique, specified thing (the year) takes the.
  1. ‘the first month’ — ordinal.
  2. ‘of the year’ — the particular year.

Answer: option (4) — The The

Q718CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q32NTA final key
Choose the correct option from the following.
Work hard lest you _________ fail.
  1. will
  2. should not
  3. could
  4. should
Concept to recalllest = ‘for fear that’; it is followed by should (or the bare subjunctive), never by a negative.
  1. ‘lest you should fail’ = so that you do not fail.
  2. ‘lest … should not’ is a double negative — the classic trap.

Answer: option (4) — should

Trap(2) adds a second negative to a word that is already negative.
Q719CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q33NTA final key
Fill in the blank with suitable word from the given options :
_________ I switch the air conditioner on ?
  1. Will
  2. Should
  3. Must
  4. Shall
Concept to recallOffers and suggestions in the first person use Shall I …?; Should I …? asks for advice and is also acceptable.
  1. An offer: ‘Shall I switch the AC on?’
  2. ‘Should I’ (asking whether it is advisable) also works.
  3. ‘Will I’ asks about the future, ‘Must I’ about obligation.

Answer: option (4) — Shall

NoteNTA’s final key accepts both (2) Should and (4) Shall.
Q720CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q12NTA final key
Passage (summarised): will our species last?

No species lasts forever. Ours has existed for at least 200,000 years, which is not old in evolutionary terms, so we should “persist” for hundreds of thousands of years more, and there is no sign that Homo sapiens is in decline. Whether we could destroy ourselves completely — by nuclear annihilation, say — is debated; some argue humans are so numerous, widespread and adaptable that no single catastrophe would wipe us out.

A collapse of global ecosystems caused by climate change and overpopulation has also been predicted as a route to our extinction, but it is hard to believe it could cause a human die-off everywhere. It is impossible to “predict” the coming centuries; yet, more than any other species, humanity can steer its own evolution through technology, genetic modification and control of resources, which makes it likely we will outlast the typical mammal species.

Choose the correct word based on your understanding of the Comprehension:
He is unable to _______ the outcome of next week’s match.
  1. Persist
  2. Predict
  3. Accept
  4. Exist
Concept to recallCollocation: one predicts an outcome; the passage says it is impossible to predict the coming centuries.
  1. ‘predict the outcome’ fits a future match.
  2. ‘Accept’ would need the outcome to have happened; persist/exist do not take an object.

Answer: option (2) — Predict

Q721CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q26NTA final key
Match the sentences in List I with their suitable Articles in List II:
LIST ILIST II
A. He is ______ best doctor in town.I. a
B. It is ____ university in Delhi.II. an
C. This is ________ bad.III. the
D. I came here ________ hour ago.IV. No article

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
  2. A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
  3. A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
  4. A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
Concept to recallthe + superlative; a before a ‘yoo’ sound (a university); an before a silent h (an hour); no article before a predicative adjective.
  1. the best doctor (A-III); a university (B-I) — ‘yoo’ is a consonant sound.
  2. This is bad (C-IV); an hour (D-II) — h is silent.

Answer: option (1) — A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

Q722CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q27NTA final key
Fill in the blanks with appropriate Articles:
It was ________ honour to meet ________ professor
  1. an, the
  2. a, a
  3. a, the
  4. an, a
Concept to recallSilent h → an honour; a particular, known person → the professor.
  1. ‘honour’ begins with a vowel sound → an.
  2. Meeting a specific professor → the. (‘an, a’ is possible in isolation, but NTA keys the definite reading.)

Answer: option (1) — an, the

Q723CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q30NTA final key
Fill in the blank with an appropriate Preposition:
The Soldiers are _____ war.
  1. at
  2. on
  3. in
  4. with
Concept to recall‘at war’ (fixed phrase, like at peace, at rest); ‘at war with’ an enemy.
  1. Being in a state of war = ‘at war’.

Answer: option (1) — at

Q724CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q31NTA final key
Fill in the blank with an appropriate Preposition:
I prefer buttermilk _________ lassi.
  1. over
  2. to
  3. in
  4. on
Concept to recallprefer X to Y (traditional grammar); ‘prefer … over’ is informal.
  1. ‘I prefer buttermilk to lassi.’
  2. ‘over’ is heard but exam grammar keys to.

Answer: option (2) — to

Trap‘over’ sounds natural in conversation.
Q725CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q32NTA final key
Fill in the blank with an appropriate Modal:
______ I ask you a question?
  1. shall
  2. will
  3. can
  4. might
Concept to recallAsking permission: Can I …? (informal) / May I …? (formal). Shall I offers to do something for the listener.
  1. Asking permission to ask → ‘Can I ask you a question?’
  2. ‘Shall I’ is an offer; ‘Will I’ asks about the future; ‘Might I’ is very formal and rare.

Answer: option (3) — can

Q726CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q33NTA final key
Fill in the blank with an appropriate Modal:
______ you like a cup of tea?
  1. would
  2. shall
  3. could
  4. may
Concept to recallPolite offers: Would you like …?
  1. ‘Would you like a cup of tea?’ is the fixed offer form.

Answer: option (1) — would

Grammar: Voice, Narration, Tense and Usage173 questions

Q727CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q16NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the most suitable word from the options given below:-
The nurse asked the patient to _____ down and take some rest for speedy recovery.
  1. lain
  2. lie
  3. lay
  4. laid
Concept to recallLie (recline, intransitive): lie – lay – lain. Lay (put something down, transitive): lay – laid – laid.
  1. “asked the patient to ___ down” – base form after to, no object ⇒ lie.
  2. “lay” needs an object; “lain/laid” are participles.

Answer: option (2) — lie

Trap“Lay down” is common in speech but wrong without an object.
Q728CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q20NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word from the options given below:
Although Sudhir did not get much time to prepare, yet he could present the topic ----------- before the board of directors.
  1. Effective
  2. Effectively
  3. Effectfully
  4. Affective
Concept to recallA verb (“present”) is modified by an adverb: effectively.
  1. How did he present? ⇒ adverb ⇒ effectively.
  2. Effective/affective are adjectives; “effectfully” is not standard English.

Answer: option (2) — Effectively

Note“Although … yet” is the sentence as printed; standard English uses only one of the two.
Q729CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q24NTA final key
Choose the option which best expresses the same sentence in Passive voice:
Every Monday, she paid him rent without fail.
  1. She had paid him rent every Monday without fail.
  2. Every Monday, he was paid rent by her without fail.
  3. Every Monday, he has been paid rent by her.
  4. He is paid rent by her, every Monday without fail.
Concept to recallSimple past active → was/were + past participle. Keep the tense and every part of the sentence.
  1. Active: simple past “paid” ⇒ passive “was paid”.
  2. Indirect object “him” becomes subject “he”; “by her”; keep “every Monday” and “without fail”.
  3. Option 1 is still active (and past perfect); 3 changes tense and drops “without fail”; 4 is present tense.

Answer: option (2) — Every Monday, he was paid rent by her without fail.

Q730CUET 2026 · 11 May, Shift 1 · Q26NTA final key
Select the option which expresses the given sentence in Indirect speech:
The visitor said to Sameer," Why did your father drag you into this situation?"
  1. The visitor said to Sameer that why his father dragged him into this situation.
  2. The visitor asked Sameer why his father dragged him into that situation?
  3. The visitor asked Sameer why his father had dragged him into that situation.
  4. The visitor told Sameer why his father had dragged him into that situation?
Concept to recallWh-question in reported speech: said to → asked; no that; statement word order; full stop; simple past → past perfect; this → that.
  1. Reporting verb: asked Sameer.
  2. “did … drag” → “had dragged”; your → his; you → him; this → that.
  3. End with a full stop, not a question mark ⇒ option 3.

Answer: option (3) — The visitor asked Sameer why his father had dragged him into that situation.

TrapOption 2 is nearly right but keeps the question mark and the simple past.
Q731CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q10NTA final key
Complete the sentence with the appropriate word from the given options:-
Her command over English is ------------------- .
  1. more excellent
  2. most excellent
  3. excellent
  4. the most excellent
Concept to recallAbsolute adjectives (excellent, perfect, unique) are not normally compared.
  1. “Excellent” already means of the highest quality – no “more/most”.
  2. No comparison is being made in the sentence anyway ⇒ excellent.

Answer: option (3) — excellent

Q732CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q24NTA final key
Choose the correct transformation of the given sentence in Indirect Speech:-
The teacher said to the boy, "Why don’t you bring your books?"
  1. The teacher said to the boy that why don't you bring your books?
  2. The teacher asked the boy why he didn't bring his books.
  3. The teacher asked the boy, why didn’t he bring your books?"
  4. The teacher asked the boy, why didn't he bring his books.
Concept to recallWh-question → asked + wh-word + subject + verb (no inversion, no comma, no question mark); present → past; you/your → he/his.
  1. said to → asked; “why don’t you bring” → “why he didn’t bring”; your → his.
  2. Options 3 and 4 keep the question order (“didn’t he”); option 1 keeps “that why” and the direct form.

Answer: option (2) — The teacher asked the boy why he didn't bring his books.

Q733CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q25NTA final key
Fill in the blanks given in List-I with the words given in List-II
List IList II
(A) He______ the television when the bell rang.(I) watch
(B) I,already, ________ this movie.(II) watching
(C) The police teams are on duty to ________ over his whereabouts.(III) have watched
(D) At this time tomorrow, you will be ____ the cricket match in London.(IV) was watching

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)
  3. (A) - (III), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (II), (C) - (I), (D) - (IV)
Concept to recallPast continuous for an action interrupted by a past event; present perfect with already; base form after to; future continuous = will be + -ing.
  1. was watching … when the bell rang (A-IV).
  2. I have already watched (B-III).
  3. to watch over = to guard (C-I).
  4. will be watching (D-II).

Answer: option (2) — (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)

Q734CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q28NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
My friend had barely __ to pull out of the garage when he realised that he had left the dog inside.
  1. had been starting
  2. have started
  3. will start
  4. started
Concept to recall“had barely + past participle … when”: after had comes the past participle (started).
  1. “had barely ___” needs a past participle ⇒ started.
  2. The other options add a second auxiliary after “had”, which is ungrammatical.

Answer: option (4) — started

Q735CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q31NTA final key
Fill in the blanks with the correct pair of words arranged sequentiallly:
I_________ now that his views on how to control pollution _____ worth listening to.
  1. am convinced, are
  2. am convinced, is
  3. was convinced, is
  4. have been convinced, is
Concept to recallSubject–verb agreement: the verb agrees with the head noun (views), not with a nearer noun (pollution). “now” signals the present.
  1. “now” ⇒ present: I am convinced.
  2. Plural subject “his views” ⇒ are worth listening to.
  3. Every other option has “is”, agreeing with “pollution”.

Answer: option (1) — am convinced, are

TrapThe nearest noun “pollution” pulls students towards “is”.
Q736CUET 2026 · 6 Jun, Shift 1 · Q8NTA final key
Choose the correct passive construction of the given sentence from the options given :-
The government will offer incentives to contractors completing high priority projects.
  1. The government will be offered incentives by contractors completing high priority projects.
  2. Contractors who complete high priority projects would offer incentives to the government.
  3. Contractors completing high priority projects would be offered incentives by the government
  4. The government would offer incentives to contractors completing high priority projects
Concept to recallPassive: the receiver becomes the subject; by + doer; verb be + past participle.
  1. Receiver = contractors ⇒ subject; doer = government ⇒ “by the government”.
  2. Only option 3 keeps the meaning in the passive.
  3. Options 1 and 2 reverse who gives to whom; option 4 is still active.

Answer: option (3) — Contractors completing high priority projects would be offered incentives by the government

NoteStrictly “will offer” becomes “will be offered”; the option prints “would”, but it is the only passive with the right meaning.
Q737CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q25NTA final key
Fill in the blanks in  List-I with the appropriate verbs from List-II.

(A) They ______ that I go with them.(I) recommended
(B) The doctor _________that I rest for two days.(II) demanded
(C) The chairperson _________ that plans be changed.(III) insisted
(D) The landlord________ that I pay the rent by Tuesday latest.(IV) proposed

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV)
  3. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (II)
Concept to recallVerbs of demand/suggestion (insist, recommend, propose, demand) take the subjunctive: “that I go”, “that plans be changed”. Choose by sense.
  1. A doctor recommends rest → B-I.
  2. A chairperson proposes a change of plans (at a meeting) → C-IV.
  3. A landlord demands rent → D-II; that leaves A-III (they insisted).
  4. ⇒ A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Q738CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q15NTA final key
Match the blanks in List-I with the Prepostions in List-II :
List-I (Sentences)List-II (Prepositions)
(A) The edited version of her article is indistinguishable __________ her first version.(I) with
(B) I just don’t feel any affinity ____________ his prose style. It’s too caustic.(II) to
(C) Her ideas are not all that dissimilar ___________ mine.(III) for
(D) It would be wrong to mistake his diffidence ___________ his arrogance or coldness.(IV) from
  1. (A) - (IV), (B) - (I), (C) - (II), (D) - (III)
  2. (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV)
  3. (A) - (IV), (B) - (II), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)
Concept to recallFixed prepositions: indistinguishable from; affinity with/for; dissimilar to/from; mistake X for Y.
  1. A indistinguishable from (IV); B affinity with (I); C dissimilar to (II); D mistake ... for (III).
  2. Options (1) and (3) both have A-IV and D-III (you mistake one thing for another); they differ on B and C, and affinity with + dissimilar to settles it: option (1).

Answer: option (1) — (A) - (IV), (B) - (I), (C) - (II), (D) - (III)

Q739CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q44NTA final key
Complete the sentences given in List-I with the appropriate adverbs given in List-II :

(B) It was a serious accident. But the car was _________ damaged.(II) reasonably
(C) The meeting was a disaster as it was very __________ organized.(III) quickly

  1. (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)
  2. (A) - (IV), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (I)
  3. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)
Concept to recallAdverbs of degree and manner; hardly = almost not (not “in a hard way”).
  1. A: reasonably affordable (II).
  2. B: serious accident but the car was hardly damaged (IV).
  3. C: disaster → badly organized (I).
  4. D: gifted → learns quickly (III).
