Q740CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q45NTA final key
Choose the appropriate word pair to complete the sentence :
I didn’t know Rahul was in the hospital. If I __________, I would __________ him.
  1. knew, go
  2. had known, have visited
  3. have known, be going
  4. know, had gone
Concept to recallThird conditional (unreal past): If + had + V3, would have + V3.
  1. The situation is past and did not happen (“I didn’t know”) → third conditional.
  2. If I had known, I would have visited him.
  3. (1) is the second conditional (present unreal).

Answer: option (2) — had known, have visited

Q741CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Code A · Q8NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
Most of the guests arrived for the concert __________ bus.
  1. by
  2. with
  3. from
  4. through
Concept to recallMeans of transport takes by with no article: by bus, by train, by air (but in the bus / on the bus).
  1. arrived ... by bus — mode of travel.
  2. with bus, through bus are unidiomatic; from bus would need an article and changes the sense.

Answer: option (1) — by

Q742CUET 2024 · 29 May (Delhi re-scheduled) · Code A · Q21NTA final key
Choose the correct expression to complete the sentence :
How _______________ your name ?
  1. is it pronounced
  2. you pronounce
  3. do you pronounce
  4. to pronounce
Concept to recallA wh-question in the simple present needs the auxiliary do/does before the subject: How do you + base verb?
  1. How do you pronounce your name?
  2. (1) leaves your name without a role (How is it pronounced, your name? is colloquial at best); (2) lacks the auxiliary; (4) is not a finite clause.

Answer: option (3) — do you pronounce

Q743CUET 2024 · 29 May (Delhi re-scheduled) · Code A · Q30NTA final key
Choose the appropriate option to complete the following sentence :
Kalyani made her children___________ chores on Sunday.
  1. make some
  2. take some
  3. do some
  4. does some
Concept to recallCausative make + object + bare infinitive; and the collocation is do chores (not make chores).
  1. made her children do some chores.
  2. does is finite and cannot follow made her children; make/take chores are wrong collocations.

Answer: option (3) — do some

Q744CUET 2024 · 29 May (Delhi re-scheduled) · Code A · Q40NTA final key
Match the blanks in List-I with the verb forms in List-II :

  1. (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

  3. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  4. (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)
Concept to recallTense markers: every day → simple present; a finished event → simple past; her whole life (up to now) → present perfect continuous; duration in the past (the whole of yesterday) → past perfect continuous.
  1. A plays (III); B played (I); C has been playing (IV); D had been playing (II).

Q745CUET 2024 · 29 May (Delhi re-scheduled) · Code A · Q42NTA final key
Complete the sentences given in List-I with the appropriate prepositions given in List-II :

  1. (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)

  3. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (II)
Concept to recallFixed prepositions: delighted with; full of; happen to someone; succeed in doing.

Q746CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q16NTA final key
Choose the correct Passive form of the sentence:
"This book will change your life".
  1. You will change your life.
  2. Book would change you and life.
  3. Your life will be changed by this book.
  4. Life is going to be changed via the book.
Concept to recallPassive of the simple future: object + will be + V3 + by + subject.
  1. Object your life becomes subject; will change → will be changed; agent by this book.
  2. The last option changes the tense (is going to) and drops your; the first two are not passive.

Answer: option (3) — Your life will be changed by this book.

Q747CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q17NTA final key
Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the following in Passive Voice.
You are teasing them.
  1. They were being teased by you.
  2. They are teased by you.
  3. They have been teasing by you.
  4. They are being teased by you.
Concept to recallPresent continuous passive: am/is/are + being + V3.
  1. are teasing (present continuous) → are being teased; them → they.
  2. The first option shifts to past; the second loses being (simple present); the third is not passive.

Answer: option (4) — They are being teased by you.

Q748CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q18NTA final key
Out of the given options, choose the Direct Speech for the sentence:-
He exclaimed sadly that he was undone.
  1. He said, 'I am undone!'
  2. He said, 'Alas! I am undone.'
  3. He said, 'Sadly I am done.'
  4. He said, 'Alas! I am done.'
Concept to recallReporting verbs like exclaimed sadly / with sorrow stand for an interjection such as Alas! in direct speech; tense moves back from was to am.
  1. “Exclaimed sadly” → Alas!; “he was undone” → “I am undone”.
  2. Done is not undone (ruined); the first option loses the sorrow.

Answer: option (2) — He said, 'Alas! I am undone.'

Q749CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q19NTA final key
Pick the correct Indirect Speech for the given sentence :
Rakesh said to Mahesh, "Go away".
  1. Rakesh asked Mahesh to go away.
  2. Rakesh ordered Mahesh to go away.
  3. Rakesh said Mahesh to go away.
  4. Rakesh wanted Mahesh to go away.
Concept to recallImperatives in indirect speech: ordered / told / requested / advised + object + to-infinitive, chosen by tone.
  1. “Go away” is a blunt command, so ordered.
  2. said Mahesh to is ungrammatical; asked suits a polite request; wanted reports a wish, not speech.

Answer: option (2) — Rakesh ordered Mahesh to go away.

Q750CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q28worked here
Convert the following sentence into its Exclamatory form:
"I wish that I were young again."
  1. Alas if I were young again!
  2. Hurrah! I could be young again!
  3. Ah! that I were young again!
  4. Oh! if I were young!
Concept to recallA wish in assertive form (“I wish that…”) becomes exclamatory as “Oh that…!” or “Would that…!”, keeping every idea of the original.
  1. The textbook pattern is O that / Ah, that I were young again! — the third option.
  2. But the first option (Alas, if I were…) is also a defensible exclamatory wish, and the fourth drops again; Hurrah expresses joy, which is wrong.
  3. Because more than one option could be argued, NTA dropped the question.

Answer: option (3) — Ah! that I were young again!

NoteNTA dropped this question in the final key (marks given to all). The answer shown is the standard textbook form.
Q751CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q29NTA final key
'What a delicious meal!' is an Exclamatory sentence for which of the following Assertive Sentences:
  1. It was what a delicious meal.
  2. The meal is very delicious.
  3. It is a meal very delicious.
  4. This were a delicious meal.
Concept to recallExclamatory ↔ assertive: What a + adj + noun! = It/The noun is very + adj.
  1. “What a delicious meal!” asserts that the meal is very delicious.
  2. The others are ungrammatical (word order, This were, “was what a”).

Answer: option (2) — The meal is very delicious.

Q752CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q34NTA final key
The first thing to be written while writing a formal letter is ______.
  1. Date
  2. Sender's Address
  3. Salutation
  4. Subject
Concept to recallFormal letter order: sender’s address → date → receiver’s address → subject → salutation → body → complimentary close → signature.
  1. The sender’s address heads the letter; the date follows it.

Answer: option (2) — Sender's Address

Q753CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q35NTA final key
Which amongst the following is NOT part of an informal letter?
  1. The address of the sender
  2. The salutation or greeting
  3. The invoice
  4. The signature
Concept to recallInformal letter parts: sender’s address, date, salutation, body, closing, signature.
  1. An invoice is a business bill, never part of a personal letter.

Answer: option (3) — The invoice

Q754CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q37NTA final key
Identify the incorrect example of Past Perfect Tense from the given options :
  1. I had gone to the gymnasium by the time you arrived.
  2. I had retired to bed when the guests arrived.
  3. I had many opportunities to swim in the past.
  4. I had just stepped into my office when the phone rang.
Concept to recallPast perfect = had + past participle (had gone, had retired). Had alone as the main verb (had many opportunities) is simple past of have.
  1. In the third sentence had is the main verb meaning “possessed”: simple past, not past perfect.
  2. The other three contain had + V3 (gone, retired, stepped).

Answer: option (3) — I had many opportunities to swim in the past.

Q755CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q46NTA final key
Out of the four alternatives, choose the one that suits the best as a question tag for the sentence:
She rarely attends the class, ______?
  1. Does she
  2. Isn't it
  3. Is it
  4. Doesn't she
Concept to recallQuestion tags: a negative-sense statement (with rarely, seldom, hardly, never) takes a positive tag; the auxiliary matches the verb (attends → does) and the pronoun matches the subject.
  1. Rarely makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive: does she?
  2. Doesn’t she ignores rarely; is it/isn’t it have the wrong auxiliary and pronoun.

Answer: option (1) — Does she

TrapMissing the negative force of rarely.
Q756CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 1 · Q50NTA final key
Choose the option that serves as an Adjective Clause in the sentence:
The boy, whom you see bowling is my cousin.
  1. whom you see bowling
  2. is my cousin
  3. the boy whom
  4. you see bowling
Concept to recallAn adjective (relative) clause begins with who/whom/whose/which/that/where/when and describes a noun.
  1. whom you see bowling describes the boy, and the relative pronoun belongs inside it.
  2. you see bowling lacks its introducing word; is my cousin is the main predicate.

Answer: option (1) — whom you see bowling

Q757CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q16NTA final key
Change the following sentence into passive voice.
I know him.
  1. He is known to me.
  2. He is known by me.
  3. He is known with me.
  4. He is known near me.
Concept to recallSome verbs take a preposition other than by in the passive: known to, pleased with, surprised at, filled with, interested in.
  1. Know takes to: He is known to me.

Answer: option (1) — He is known to me.

TrapAutomatic by — “known by me”.
Q758CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q17NTA final key
Change the following sentence from active to passive voice :
Careless driving causes many accidents.
  1. Many accidents is caused by careless driving.
  2. Many accidents are caused by careless driving.
  3. Many accidents causes careless driving.
  4. Many accidents are causes by careless driving.
Concept to recallSimple present passive: is/are + V3; the verb agrees with the new (plural) subject.
  1. New subject many accidents is plural → are caused.
  2. is caused breaks agreement; are causes uses the wrong verb form; the third reverses the meaning.

Answer: option (2) — Many accidents are caused by careless driving.

Q759CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q18NTA final key
Change the following statement to direct speech :
He asked me what I wanted.
  1. He said to me, "What I want ?"
  2. He said to me, "What do you want ?"
  3. He said to me, "What he wants ?"
  4. He said to me, "What will you want ?"
Concept to recallReported question → direct: restore question word order (wh-word + do/does + subject + verb), present tense, and the speaker’s pronouns (I said to me → you).
  1. “what I wanted” → “What do you want?”
  2. The first and third keep statement word order; the fourth changes the tense to future.

Answer: option (2) — He said to me, "What do you want ?"

Q760CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q19NTA final key
Choose the option which best expresses the given sentence in indirect speech :
I said to Bob, "Can you complete this work by tomorrow ?"
  1. I asked Bob whether he could complete this work by the next day ?
  2. I asked Bob whether he could complete this work by tomorrow.
  3. I asked Bob whether he could complete that work by the next day.
  4. I asked Bob whether he could complete that work by the next day ?
Concept to recallIndirect yes/no question: asked + if/whether; can → could; this → that; tomorrow → the next day; full stop, not a question mark.
  1. All four changes are needed: could, that, the next day, and a full stop.
  2. The second keeps this and tomorrow; the first and fourth end with a question mark.

Answer: option (3) — I asked Bob whether he could complete that work by the next day.

NoteCollegedunia gives the second option; NTA’s key gives the third, which applies every reporting rule.
Q761CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q28NTA final key
Choose the correct option for the transformation of the given sentence into an exclamatory sentence :
He met with an accident and died.
  1. Oh ! He met with an accident and died.
  2. Alas ! He met with an accident and died.
  3. Alas ! What a terrible accident he met with.
  4. Ohho, What a terrible accident !
Concept to recallAssertive → exclamatory: add the interjection that fits the emotion — Alas! for sorrow, Hurrah! for joy, Oh! for surprise — and keep the full content.
  1. Death calls for sorrow: Alas!, keeping “met with an accident and died”.
  2. The third and fourth drop the death (and add terrible); Oh! expresses surprise, not grief.

Answer: option (2) — Alas ! He met with an accident and died.

Q762CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q29NTA final key
Choose the correct option for the transformation of the given sentence into an exclamatory sentence :
She is a wonderful woman.
  1. What a wonderful woman she is !
  2. Oh ! She is wonderful.
  3. Hurrah ! She is a wonderful woman.
  4. What ! A wonderful woman she is.
Concept to recallX is a very/an adj + noun → What a/an adj + noun + X is!
  1. “What a wonderful woman she is!” is the standard pattern.
  2. The second drops woman and ends with a full stop; Hurrah is for victory/joy; the fourth is mispunctuated.

Answer: option (1) — What a wonderful woman she is !

Q763CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q33NTA final key
Which of the following sentences have modal verbs ?
(A) Rohit comes to the class regularly.
(B) Meenal sits to sing every morning.
(C) We must respect our parents.
(D) Mohan will visit the doctor after work.
(E) Maghna's visit to the institute was fruitless.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A) and (D) Only
  2. (D) and (E) Only
  3. (A) and (C) Only
  4. (C) and (D) Only
Concept to recallModals: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to — always followed by a bare verb.
  1. (C) must and (D) will are modals.
  2. (A), (B), (E) have only ordinary verbs (comes, sits, was).

Answer: option (4) — (C) and (D) Only

Q764CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q34NTA final key
Choose the correct option given below for the format of writing an informal letter :
(A) date and salutation
(B) sender's address
(C) signing off
(D) body of the letter
(E) signature of the sender
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (B), (E), (A), (C), (D)
  2. (B), (A), (D), (C), (E)
  3. (A), (B), (C), (D), (E)
  4. (D), (A), (B), (C), (E)
Concept to recallInformal letter: sender’s address → date → salutation → body → signing off → signature.
  1. B, A, D, C, E.

Answer: option (2) — (B), (A), (D), (C), (E)

Q765CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q35NTA final key
When you are writing a formal letter to a company, what information do you include :
  1. Your address
  2. Your date of birth
  3. Both your address and the Company's address
  4. None of these
Concept to recallA formal letter carries the sender’s address and the receiver’s (inside) address.
  1. Both addresses appear; date of birth never does.

Answer: option (3) — Both your address and the Company's address

Q766CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q44NTA final key
Find out the adverb from the given sentence and tick the correct option given below :
I go to church daily and rarely fail to reach office on time.
  1. daily, rarely
  2. daily, on time
  3. rarely, go
  4. rarely, fail
Concept to recallAdverbs modify verbs and answer how often / when / how: daily (how often I go), rarely (how often I fail).
  1. daily modifies go; rarely modifies fail.
  2. go and fail are verbs; on time is an adverbial phrase, not a single adverb.

Answer: option (1) — daily, rarely

Q767CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q46NTA final key
Complete the following sentence by using a question tag :
I am older to you ______.
  1. aren't you ?
  2. aren't we ?
  3. aren't I ?
  4. can't I ?
Concept to recallTag rule: repeat the subject and auxiliary. The negative tag of I am is the special form aren’t I?
  1. Subject I, auxiliary am, positive statement → negative tag aren’t I?
  2. you/we change the subject; can’t changes the auxiliary.

Answer: option (3) — aren't I ?

NoteCollegedunia gives aren’t you?, which changes the subject; NTA’s key is aren’t I? (The sentence itself should read “older than you”; that is a slip in the paper.)
Q768CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 1 · Q50NTA final key
Pick the sentences with an Adjective Clause.
(A) I don't know whose books are kept here.
(B) I am glad that he won the match.
(C) I missed the flight as I was late.
(D) I know the place where they will come.
(E) I remember the day when we met for the first time.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A) and (B) Only
  2. (B) and (C) Only
  3. (C) and (D) Only
  4. (D) and (E) Only
Concept to recallAdjective clause = describes a noun just before it. A clause that is the object of a verb (know whose…) is a noun clause; one giving a reason (as I was late) is an adverb clause.
  1. (D) where they will come describes the place; (E) when we met… describes the day: adjective clauses.
  2. (A) and (B) are noun clauses (object of know; complement of glad); (C) is an adverb clause of reason.

Answer: option (4) — (D) and (E) Only

NoteCollegedunia gives (A) and (B); NTA’s key gives (D) and (E).
Q769CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q16NTA final key
Change the following sentence into active voice by choosing the correct option.
All his calculations have been proved wrong.
  1. It has proved all his calculations wrong.
  2. They have proved all his calculations wrong.
  3. We have proved all his calculations wrong.
  4. All his calculations were proved wrong.
Concept to recallPassive with no agent → active with an indefinite subject (they/someone); keep the tense (present perfect: have + V3).
  1. No doer is named, so supply the indefinite ‘they’.
  2. Present perfect passive ‘have been proved’ → ‘have proved’.

Answer: option (2) — They have proved all his calculations wrong.

Trap(4) is still passive (and changes the tense); ‘we’ adds a specific doer the sentence never names.
Q770CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q17NTA final key
Select the appropriate option to convert the following into active voice.
“Why was such a letter written by your brother ?”
  1. Why has such letter been written by your brother ?
  2. Why did your brother wrote such a letter ?
  3. Why did your brother write such a letter ?
  4. Why was such a letter being written by your brother ?
Concept to recallSimple past passive question → Wh- + did + subject + V1.
  1. Agent ‘your brother’ becomes subject; ‘was written’ (past) → ‘did … write’.

Answer: option (3) — Why did your brother write such a letter ?

TrapAfter did the verb is the base form — ‘did … wrote’ is wrong.
Q771CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q18NTA final key
Choose the option to correctly change the following from direct to indirect speech.
“Are you free tomorrow ?” She said to me.
  1. She told me are you free tomorrow.
  2. She asked me if I was free tomorrow.
  3. She asked me if I was free the next day.
  4. She ordered and asked if I was free tomorrow.
Concept to recallYes/no question → asked + if/whether; past reporting verb shifts tense back and tomorrow → the next day.
  1. said to → asked; add ‘if’; ‘are you’ → ‘I was’; tomorrow → the next day.

Answer: option (3) — She asked me if I was free the next day.

Trap(2) forgets to change ‘tomorrow’.
Q772CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q19NTA final key
Select the appropriate option as the conversion for the following statement into indirect speech.
- Fiona said, “It’s getting late” -
  1. Fiona said it meant to be late.
  2. Fiona said it had been late.
  3. Fiona said it has been getting late.
  4. Fiona said that it was getting late.
Concept to recallPast reporting verb: present continuous → past continuous (is getting → was getting).
  1. ‘It is getting late’ → ‘that it was getting late’.

Answer: option (4) — Fiona said that it was getting late.

Q773CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q26NTA final key
Fill in the blank with a suitable determiner.
The class will be divided into three sections and __________ section will contain 20 students.
  1. each
  2. every
  3. both
  4. All of the above
Concept to recallEach = every one of a definite, usually small, group taken individually; every stresses the whole of a larger group; both = two only.
  1. Three known sections, considered one by one → each.

Answer: option (1) — each

Trap‘Both’ refers to two, not three.
Q774CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q27NTA final key
Choose the correct form of the article which needs to the inserted in the sentence given below:
The Sun did not rise till six in __________ morning.
  1. a
  2. an
  3. the
  4. no article
Concept to recallParts of the day take the: in the morning, in the evening.
  1. Fixed phrase: ‘in the morning’.

Answer: option (3) — the

Q775CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q28NTA final key
Choose the correct exclamatory form of the following sentence from the options given below :
The students are excited to go for the excursion.
  1. How excited the students are to go on an excursion !
  2. Alas, the students are eager to go for the excursion !
  3. How the students were excited for the excursion !
  4. Kudos to the students excited to go for the excursion !
Concept to recallAssertive → exclamatory: How + adjective + subject + verb !; keep the tense and meaning.
  1. ‘are excited’ → ‘How excited the students are … !’

Answer: option (1) — How excited the students are to go on an excursion !

Trap‘Alas’ expresses sorrow; (3) changes the tense.
Q776CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q29NTA final key
Choose the correct exclamatory sentence for the following sentence :
It is a matter of regret that your grandfather has passed away.
  1. It is a regrettable that your grandfather has passed away !
  2. Oh ! We lost your grandfather !
  3. How regretful are we to lose your grandfather !
  4. Alas ! You have lost your grandfather !
Concept to recallRegret/sorrow in an assertive sentence → the interjection Alas !
  1. ‘It is a matter of regret’ becomes ‘Alas !’; keep ‘your grandfather’ and the present perfect.

Answer: option (4) — Alas ! You have lost your grandfather !

Trap(2) changes whose loss it is (‘we’) and the tense.
Q777CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q30NTA final key
Use suitable prepositions in the following sentence.
“The exercise was written __________ me __________ a Parker pen.”
  1. by, through
  2. for, by
  3. for, from
  4. by, with
Concept to recallPassive: by + the doer; with + the instrument used.
  1. Written by me (agent), with a Parker pen (instrument).

Answer: option (4) — by, with

Q778CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q31NTA final key
Choose a suitable preposition to fill in the blank :
Hereafter Raju is disqualified __________ holding any government post.
  1. from
  2. against
  3. with
  4. by
Concept to recallFixed preposition: disqualified from (doing something).
  1. disqualify someone from holding a post.

Answer: option (1) — from

Q779CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q32NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the suitable option from the list below :
“You __________ stood by your brother.”
  1. should have
  2. may have
  3. shall have
  4. might have
Concept to recallshould have + V3 = a past duty that was not done (reproach).
  1. The speaker blames the listener for not supporting his brother → ‘should have stood by’.

Answer: option (1) — should have

Trap‘may/might have’ express only possibility, not obligation.
Q780CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q33NTA final key
Choose the correct modal to fill in the blank, in the sentence given below :
When I was in college I __________ play cricket.
  1. may
  2. used to
  3. must
  4. dare to
Concept to recallused to + V1 = a past habit that no longer continues.
  1. ‘When I was in college’ signals a past habit → used to play.

Answer: option (2) — used to

Q781CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q46NTA final key
Add a suitable question tag to the following sentence from the options given below :
Mohit lives in the city.
  1. Did he ?
  2. Does he ?
  3. Will he ?
  4. Doesn’t he ?
Concept to recallPositive statement → negative tag, using the auxiliary of the tense (simple present: do/does).
  1. Positive, simple present, third person singular → doesn’t he?

Answer: option (4) — Doesn’t he ?

Q782CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q47NTA final key
Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct option :
I am tired as __________ since 7 o’clock in the morning.
  1. I have been working
  2. working
  3. I had been working
  4. I will be working
Concept to recallAction begun in the past and continuing to now, with since → present perfect continuous.
  1. ‘I am tired’ (now) + ‘since 7’ → I have been working.

Answer: option (1) — I have been working

TrapPast perfect continuous needs a past reference point, which this sentence does not have.
Q783CUET 2023 · 7 Jun, Shift 2 · Q50NTA final key
Match the sentence in List - I with the clause used in it in List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) The boy who came here is my brother.(I) Noun clause
(B) I want to know who came here.(II) Adjective clause
(C) I had left the room when my mother came to meet me.(III) Adverb clause
(D) Please tell me who came to meet me.(IV) Noun clause
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  2. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
  3. (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
  4. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
Concept to recallAdjective clause describes a noun (who after a noun); noun clause is object/subject; adverb clause tells when/why/how.
  1. A: ‘who came here’ describes ‘the boy’ → adjective (II).
  2. B and D: the clause is the object of know / tell → noun (I, IV).
  3. C: ‘when my mother came’ tells time → adverb (III).

Answer: option (4) — (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

Q784CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q16NTA final key
Mark the correct Active Voice of the following:
“The wall is being built by the mason.”
  1. The mason has built this wall.
  2. The mason is building the wall.
  3. The mason was building the wall.
  4. The mason built this wall.
Concept to recallPresent continuous passive (is being + V3) ↔ present continuous active (is + V-ing).
  1. is being built → is building; the mason becomes subject.

Answer: option (2) — The mason is building the wall.

Q785CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q17NTA final key
Choose the option which best expresses the same sentence in Passive Voice.
Somebody cleans the room every day.
  1. The room is cleaned every day.
  2. The room is being cleaned every day.
  3. The room has been cleaned every day.
  4. The room is being cleaned every day by somebody.
Concept to recallSimple present active → is/am/are + V3; an indefinite agent (somebody, people) is dropped.
  1. cleans (simple present) → is cleaned; drop ‘by somebody’.

Answer: option (1) — The room is cleaned every day.

Trap‘is being cleaned’ is present continuous — wrong tense.
Q786CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q18NTA final key
Change the following to Direct Speech by choosing the correct answer from the options given:
The judge asked the thief what he had been doing with his hand in the gentleman’s pocket.
  1. The judge said to the thief, “What were you doing with your hand in the gentleman’s pocket?”
  2. The judge said to the gentleman, “What was the thief doing in your pocket with his hand ?”
  3. The judge said to the thief, “What are you doing with your hand in the gentleman’s pocket?”
  4. The judge asked the thief, “Why are you putting your hand in the gentleman’s pocket?”
Concept to recallIndirect → direct: reverse the backshift. Past perfect continuous (had been doing) goes back to past continuous (were doing).
  1. had been doing → were doing; he/his → you/your; the question form returns.

Answer: option (1) — The judge said to the thief, “What were you doing with your hand in the gentleman’s pocket?”

Trap(3) uses present continuous: that would have become ‘was doing’, not ‘had been doing’.
Q787CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q19NTA final key
Choose the correct option to change the following question into Indirect Speech.
Julia said that she could not attend our wedding.
  1. Julia said, “ I could not attend your wedding.”
  2. Julia said, “I will not attend your wedding.”
  3. Julia said, “I am not attending your wedding.”
  4. Julia said, “I cannot attend your wedding.”
Concept to recallReported could comes from direct can; our (listener’s side) becomes your in Julia’s mouth.
  1. The sentence given is already indirect; the options are direct speech.
  2. could not → cannot; she → I; our → your.

Answer: option (4) — Julia said, “I cannot attend your wedding.”

NoteThe instruction says ‘into Indirect Speech’ but the task is really the reverse (indirect → direct).
Q788CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q26NTA final key
Choose the correct option from the words given below:
_______ child has to bring Rs. 500/- for the trip.
  1. Every
  2. Each
  3. Both
  4. All
Concept to recallEach treats members of a definite group one by one; both needs two and a plural noun; all needs a plural here.
  1. Singular noun ‘child’ rules out Both and All.
  2. The requirement is laid on every member of the known group individually → NTA keys Each.

Answer: option (2) — Each

Note‘Every child has to bring…’ is also grammatical; NTA’s final key accepts only Each.
Q789CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q27NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the appropriate pair of articles from the options given below.
“He would make _____ better statesman than _____ University Professor.”
  1. a , an
  2. the , an
  3. a , the
  4. a , a
Concept to recalla/an depends on the first sound: University begins with a ‘yoo’ (consonant) sound → a.
  1. a better statesman; a University Professor.

Answer: option (4) — a , a

TrapThe vowel letter U tempts an.
Q790CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q28NTA final key
Choose the correct conversion of the following Assertive sentence to Exclamatory sentence:
It is sad, we have lost the match.
  1. Alas! we lost the match.
  2. Alas! we have lost the match.
  3. Alas! we had lost the match.
  4. Alas! the match had been lost.
Concept to recallSorrow → Alas!; keep the original tense (present perfect).
  1. ‘It is sad’ → Alas!; keep ‘we have lost the match’.

Answer: option (2) — Alas! we have lost the match.

Q791CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q29NTA final key
Choose the correct form of the Assertive sentence for the following Exclamatory sentence:
If only I were young again!
  1. I were young again.
  2. I wished I were young again.
  3. I wish I were young again.
  4. I had wished I were young again.
Concept to recallIf only …! → I wish … (present wish about an unreal situation, subjunctive were).
  1. The wish is present → I wish I were young again.

Answer: option (3) — I wish I were young again.

Q792CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q30NTA final key
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
The assignment must be submitted ____ next Monday.
  1. for
  2. in
  3. to
  4. by
Concept to recallby + time = not later than (a deadline).
  1. Deadline → by next Monday.

Answer: option (4) — by

Q793CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q31NTA final key
From the options below, choose the correct preposition to fill in the blank:
After the party, Sumit returned home _____ car.
  1. from
  2. by
  3. to
  4. into
Concept to recallMeans of transport without an article: by car/bus/train (but in his car, on foot).
  1. returned home by car.

Answer: option (2) — by

Q794CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 2 · Q32NTA final key
Fill in the blank with a suitable Modal. Choose the correct option from the options given below:
_______ I have another cup of tea? It is very chilly outside.
  1. will
  2. can
  3. must
  4. could

Q812CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 3 · Q5NTA final key
Passage (summarised): water and sleep for teenagers

Since the body is about two-thirds water, staying hydrated matters. The British Nutrition Foundation advises teenagers to drink six to eight glasses of water a day, and more if they play sport or are very active. 100 per cent fruit juice and low-fat milk are other good sources of fluid. Sugary and caffeinated drinks “should be limited or eliminated” from the diet because they give excess sugar and empty calories.

The Cleveland Clinic says teenagers need at least nine hours of sleep a night. That is hard because of early school start times, late-afternoon practices and hours of homework. The advice: keep a regular bedtime that allows nine hours before getting up for school, and plan at least an hour of “quiet time” before bed, with all electronics “to be turned off for the night” so brain and body relax — for example by listening to soothing music or reading a book.

Concept to recallSpot the marker word in each phrase: a modal (should), adjectives before a noun (sugary, caffeinated), an adverb in -ly (completely), and be + V3 (to be turned).
  1. should → modal (A-II); sugary, caffeinated → adjectives (B-III); completely → adverb (C-I); to be turned off → passive (D-IV).

Q818CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 1 · Q24NTA final key
Change the following sentence from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:
The coach promised," If you will come before school tomorrow, I will teach it,"

  2. The coach promised that if came before school the next day, he would teach it to me.
  3. The coach promised to come before school and teach it to me.
  4. The coach promised that I will be thought before school if I came
Concept to recallReported speech: the reporting verb carries the tone (applauded, exclaimed, promised); tenses go one step back; pronouns and time words shift (you → he/she, tomorrow → the next day).
  1. Reporting verb promised + that; will → would; tomorrow → the next day; I (coach) → he; you → the listener (me).
  2. Only (2) keeps both the condition and the promise (its missing I after if is a printing slip).
  3. (1) and (3) change who comes and when; (4) keeps will and misspells taught.

Q819CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 1 · Q25NTA final key
Change the following sentence from Indirect speech to Direct Speech.

  3. She was happy that he had done better than last time.

Concept to recallReported speech: the reporting verb carries the tone (applauded, exclaimed, promised); tenses go one step back; pronouns and time words shift (you → he/she, tomorrow → the next day). An interjection (Bravo!) is dropped and its feeling goes into the reporting verb.
  1. (The instruction is printed back to front: the sentence is direct, the options are indirect.)
  2. Bravo! expresses praise → reporting verb applauded.
  3. did → had done; you → he.
  4. (2) keeps the interjection as a word; (3) and (4) add feelings (happiness, disbelief) not in the original.

Answer: option (1) — She applauded him, saying that he had done better than last time.

Q831CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q21NTA final key
Choose the option that demonstrates the most appropriate use of articles
  1. The Secretary and a Treasurer are absent
  2. The Secretary and the Treasurer are absent
  3. Secretary and Treasurer are absent
  4. The Secretary and Treasurer are absent
Concept to recallTwo different persons → article before each noun, plural verb; one person holding two posts → one article, singular verb (The Secretary and Treasurer is absent).
  1. The verb are tells us two persons, so each noun takes the: The Secretary and the Treasurer are absent.
  2. (4) would mean one person, which clashes with are.

Answer: option (2) — The Secretary and the Treasurer are absent

Trap(4) is the one-person form; with are it is inconsistent.
Q832CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q27NTA final key
Choosing the most appropriate answer from the given list. Convert the following sentence in Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.
"I am guilty", the defended said.
  1. The defendant admitted that he was guilty
  2. The defendant accepted his guilt
  3. The defendant said yes he was guilty
  4. The guilty defendant accepted his fault
Concept to recallReported speech: the reporting verb carries the tone (applauded, exclaimed, promised); tenses go one step back; pronouns and time words shift (you → he/she, tomorrow → the next day).
  1. A confession is best reported with admitted; I am → he was; join with that.
  2. (2) and (4) summarise without a reported clause; (3) inserts yes.

Answer: option (1) — The defendant admitted that he was guilty

Q833CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q28NTA final key
Choosing the most appropriate answer from the given list, convert the following sentence in Indirect speech to Direct speech.
I asked Sara whether Bill had given her that ring.
  1. "Did Bill willing to give that ring?, "I asked Sara.
  2. "Did Bill give you that ring?", I asked Sara.
  3. "Can Bill give you a ring?", I asked Sara.
  4. "Should Bill give you rings?", I asked Sara.
Concept to recallReported speech: the reporting verb carries the tone (applauded, exclaimed, promised); tenses go one step back; pronouns and time words shift (you → he/she, tomorrow → the next day).
  1. whether → a yes/no question; had given → did … give; her → you; that ring stays.
  2. (3) and (4) change the modal and the meaning.

Answer: option (2) — "Did Bill give you that ring?", I asked Sara.

Q834CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q29NTA final key
Convert the following Exclamatory Sentence to Assertive Sentence:
What a Lovely House!
  1. Oh! What a lovely house!
  2. The house that I am looking at is very lonely
  3. It was a very lovely house indeed
  4. What a lovely house am I looking at
Concept to recallExclamatory → assertive: drop What a …! and state the fact with very/indeed.
  1. (3) is the only plain statement keeping lovely.
  2. (1) and (4) are still exclamatory; (2) changes lovely to lonely.

Answer: option (3) — It was a very lovely house indeed

Traplonely vs lovely — a look-alike trap.
Q835CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q32NTA final key
Choose the best option to convert the given Assertive Sentence into Exclamatory Sentence:
I wish I knew more people here.
  1. If only I knew more people here!
  2. What a pity to have known more people here.
  3. Oh! Fie! I know nobody here.
  4. Alas! I could have known more people here.
Concept to recallA wish becomes exclamatory with If only …! or Would that …!
  1. If only I knew more people here! keeps the same wish and tense.
  2. The others change the meaning (regret about the past, contempt).

Answer: option (1) — If only I knew more people here!

NoteThe same item, with partly different options, was set on 18 Jun Shift 1 (Q28).
Q836CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q33NTA final key
Fill in the appropriate modals in List I with the sentences given in List II
LIST ILIST II
A. How _____ you shout at your best friend?I. can
B. ____ we go to the beach then?II. should
C. No one _______ question the ways of GodIII. shall
D. We _____ respect our eldersIV. could
  1. A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
  2. A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
  3. A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
  4. A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
Concept to recallModals: can = ability/possibility/permission; could = past ability, polite request, unreal wish; shall = future with I/we, offers and suggestions (“Shall I…?”); should / ought to = duty, advice; would = polite offer (“Would you like…?”).
  1. A: How could you shout …? — reproach (IV).
  2. B: Shall we go to the beach then? — suggestion (III).
  3. C: No one can question the ways of God (I).
  4. D: We should respect our elders — duty (II).

Answer: option (3) — A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

Q837CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q34NTA final key
Fill in the blank with a proper modal so that the sentence sounds like a promise.
I ______ help you.
  1. might
  2. shouldn't
  3. can
  4. will
Concept to recallwill with I expresses willingness, a promise.
  1. I will help you = a promise.
  2. can = ability; might = mere possibility.

Answer: option (4) — will

Q838CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q35NTA final key
Identify the Adjective Clause in the following sentence.
"The spot where the battle was fought is unknown".
  1. The spot where
  2. where the battle was fought
  3. The spot where the battle was fought
  4. the battle was
Concept to recallAn adjective (relative) clause describes a noun and begins with a relative word (who, which, that, where, when).
  1. The clause describing spot is where the battle was fought — it has its own subject and verb.
  2. The spot where the battle was fought is the whole subject (noun + its clause).
  3. NTA’s final key gives option (3).

Answer: option (3) — The spot where the battle was fought

NoteStrictly the adjective clause is option (2), where the battle was fought; option (3) adds the noun it qualifies. NTA’s final key (and the revised key of Feb 2024) gives (3); kept here.
Q839CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q48NTA final key
Identify the type of adverb in the following sentence.
"I therefore left my apartment".
  1. Adverb of frequency
  2. Adverb of manner
  3. Adverb of reason
  4. Adverb of Time
Concept to recalltherefore, hence, consequently = adverbs of reason/result.
  1. therefore answers “why?” → adverb of reason.

Answer: option (3) — Adverb of reason

Q840CUET 2023 · 18 Jun, Shift 3 · Q49NTA final key
Fill in the blank with an appropriate adverb.
They have ______ faith in their Guru.
  1. Fairly good
  2. wholly
  3. very
  4. too much
Concept to recallBefore a noun (faith) we need a quantity word: much / too much / great; very cannot modify a noun.
  1. They have too much faith in their Guru is grammatical.
  2. very faith and wholly faith are ungrammatical; fairly good faith means honesty, not belief.

Answer: option (4) — too much

Q841CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q16NTA final key
Choose the correct option which best expresses the following sentence in Active Voice :
He was appointed chairman.
  1. They appointed him chairman
  2. You appointed him chairman
  3. He appointed chairman
  4. Chairman appointed him
Concept to recallActive → passive: object becomes subject, verb becomes be + past participle in the same tense, the doer goes into a by-phrase in the object case (by me, by him). When the passive names no doer, use an indefinite subject (they, someone) in the active.
  1. No doer given → supply They; was appointed → appointed; He → him.
  2. You introduces a specific doer that is not in the original.

Answer: option (1) — They appointed him chairman

Q842CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q17NTA final key
Choose the correct option which best expresses the following sentence in Passive Voice.
My father will write a letter.
  1. A letter was written by my father.
  2. A letter will have been written by my father
  3. A letter is neither by my father
  4. A letter will be written by my father
Concept to recallActive → passive: object becomes subject, verb becomes be + past participle in the same tense, the doer goes into a by-phrase in the object case (by me, by him).
  1. Simple future will write → will be written.
  2. (2) is future perfect; (1) is past.

Answer: option (4) — A letter will be written by my father

Trap(2) adds a perfect tense not in the original.
Q843CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q18NTA final key
Choose the correct option which best expresses the following same sentence in Indirect speech.
Anil said, "Ali deserved the prize".
  1. Anil says that Ali deserves the prize.
  2. Anil said that Ali deserves the prize.
  3. Anil said that Ali has deserved the prize.
  4. Anil said that Ali had deserved the prize.
Concept to recallReported speech: the reporting verb carries the tone (applauded, exclaimed, promised); tenses go one step back; pronouns and time words shift (you → he/she, tomorrow → the next day).
  1. Past reporting verb said → simple past deserved moves back to past perfect had deserved.

Answer: option (4) — Anil said that Ali had deserved the prize.

Q844CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q19NTA final key
Choose the option which best expresses the following sentence in Direct speech :
The speaker said that two wrongs do not make a right.
  1. The speaker said, "Two wrongs do not make a right".
  2. The speaker said, "Don't make two wrongs right".
  3. The speaker said, "What wrongs ! did not make right
  4. The speaker said , "Two wrongs and not to make a right".
Concept to recallA universal truth or proverb keeps its present tense in reported speech, so the direct form is the same words in quotation marks.
  1. Two wrongs do not make a right is a proverb; quote it unchanged.

Answer: option (1) — The speaker said, "Two wrongs do not make a right".

Q845CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q28NTA final key
Select the most appropriate Exclamatory form of the sentence :
It was very foolish of me to throw my mobile.
  1. How foolish I am that I threw my mobile!
  2. I am a fool to throw my mobile!
  3. Am I that foolish to throw my mobile!
  4. How foolish of me to throw my mobile!
Concept to recallAssertive with very + adjective → exclamatory with How + adjective … !
  1. very foolish of me → How foolish of me to throw my mobile!
  2. The other options change the structure or the tense.

Q846CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q29NTA final key
Select the most appropriate Exclamatory form of the sentence given below :
I wish I were an astronaut.
  1. I wish that I was an astronaut!
  2. I wish that I could be an astronaut!
  3. Oh that I were an astronaut!
  4. Alas! I were an astronaut!
Concept to recallA wish becomes exclamatory with Oh that …! / Would that …! / If only …!
  1. Oh that I were an astronaut!
  2. (1) and (2) still use I wish; (4) Alas expresses sorrow, not a wish.

Q847CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q32NTA final key
Select the most appropriate Modal to be filled in the blank in the sentence given below :
I _________ visit my friend daily when she was in the hospital.
  1. can
  2. used to
  3. should
  4. could
Concept to recallused to = a past habit or repeated action.
  1. daily + past time (when she was in the hospital) → past habit: used to.
  2. could is past ability, which does not fit a statement of what one regularly did.

Answer: option (2) — used to

Q848CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q33NTA final key
Select the appropriate Modal to fill in the blank in the sentence given below :
Since the remote is with my mother, I _________ not switch on the T.V.
  1. could
  2. would
  3. might
  4. can
Concept to recallcan / cannot = present ability or possibility.
  1. is sets the sentence in the present, so present can not (cannot).
  2. could would need a past context.

Q849CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q44NTA final key
Identify the sentence in which an Adverb of Manner has been used :
  1. She dances very skillfuly.
  2. My brother comes often every Sunday.
  3. He briefly narrated the incident to me.
  4. He goes usually to the movie every Friday.
Concept to recallAdverbs of manner answer “how?”; often, usually are adverbs of frequency.
  1. briefly tells how he narrated → manner, and the sentence is correct.
  2. (1) also has an adverb of manner but misspells skilfully; (2) and (4) use frequency adverbs, wrongly placed.

Answer: option (3) — He briefly narrated the incident to me.

Trap(1) is a manner adverb too, but misspelt (skillfuly).
Q850CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q46NTA final key
Select the appropriate question tag for the given sentence :
It looks perfect here.
  1. is it ?
  2. isn't it ?
  3. does it ?
  4. doesn't it ?
Concept to recallPositive statement → negative tag; with no auxiliary in the statement, the tag uses do/does/did.
  1. looks (simple present, third person) → tag doesn’t it?

Answer: option (4) — doesn't it ?

Trapisn’t it? is the common spoken error; there is no is in the sentence.
Q851CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q47NTA final key
Select the correct option to make the (grammatically correct) sentence.
_________ we had to cancel the trip.
  1. Being a rainy day
  2. Having been a rainy day
  3. It had been a rainy day
  4. It being a rainy day
Concept to recallA participle phrase must share the subject of the main clause; if it does not, give it its own subject (absolute construction: It being a rainy day, …).
  1. Being a rainy day, we … would say we were a rainy day — a dangling participle.
  2. Adding It makes an absolute phrase: It being a rainy day, we had to cancel the trip.
  3. (3) is a full clause and would need a conjunction.

Answer: option (4) — It being a rainy day

Trap(1) is the dangling-participle trap.
Q852CUET 2023 · 19 Jun, Shift 2 · Q50NTA final key
Identify the Adjective clause in the following sentence :
A man whose habits are industrious, is sure to succeed.
  1. A man
  2. is sure to succeed
  3. whose habits are industrious
  4. is sure
Concept to recallAn adjective clause qualifies a noun and opens with a relative word (who, whose, which, that, where).
  1. whose habits are industrious describes A man and has its own verb are.

Answer: option (3) — whose habits are industrious

Q853CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q16NTA final key
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence -
Who asked you to drive my car ?
  1. By who you are asked to drive my car ?
  2. By whom you were asked to drive my car ?
  3. By whom you were asked to drive my car.
  4. By whom were you asked to drive my car ?
Concept to recall‘Who + past verb?’ → ‘By whom + was/were + subject + V3?’ (question order kept).
  1. who becomes by whom; tense stays simple past → were … asked.
  2. A question keeps the auxiliary before the subject: ‘were you’.
  3. (2) and (3) use statement order; (1) uses who and the present tense.

Answer: option (4) — By whom were you asked to drive my car ?

Q854CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q17NTA final key
Choose the correct option which best expresses the same sentence in passive/Active Voice ?
The packet has not been opened by any one.
  1. Anyone has not opened the packet.
  2. No one has opened the packet.
  3. No one has not opened the packet.
  4. No one has been opening the packet.
Concept to recall‘not … by anyone’ becomes the subject ‘No one’ with a positive verb (no double negative).
  1. Present perfect passive → present perfect active: has opened.
  2. ‘not … anyone’ → ‘No one’. (1) starts with ‘Anyone … not’ (unidiomatic); (3) is a double negative; (4) changes the tense.

Answer: option (2) — No one has opened the packet.

Q855CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q20NTA final key
Choose the correct option for the given sentence to transform it into the Indirect form :
She tells me, “I have no interest in serious fiction”.
  1. She tells me that I had no interest in serious fiction
  2. She tells me that she has not interest in serious fiction
  3. She told me that she had no interest in serious fiction
  4. She tells me that I have no interest in serious fiction
Concept to recallPronoun change: the speaker’s I becomes she. With a present reporting verb (tells) the tense would not change.
  1. I → she, which rules out (1) and (4).
  2. Strictly, ‘She tells me that she has no interest …’ is right, but (2) spoils it with ‘has not interest’.
  3. That leaves (3), the past-tense version, as the only grammatical option.

Answer: option (3) — She told me that she had no interest in serious fiction

NoteWith tells (present) the tense should stay present; NTA keys (3), whose reporting verb is in the past, because (2) is ungrammatical.
Q856CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q21NTA final key
Choose the correct option which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech
She said that she really liked the furniture.
  1. “She really liked this furniture,” she said.
  2. “She liked really this furniture,” she said.
  3. “I really like this furniture,” she said.
  4. “I have really liked this furniture,” she said.
Concept to recallIndirect → direct: she → I, past → present (liked → like), the → this.
  1. The speaker refers to herself as I; the simple past returns to simple present.
  2. (1), (2) keep she; (4) uses the present perfect.

Answer: option (3) — “I really like this furniture,” she said.

Q857CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q28NTA final key
Change the following Assertive sentence into Exclamatory sentence.
It is sad that we lost the game today.
  1. It is pity we lost!
  2. It is sad today we lost!
  3. Lost! we today.
  4. Alas! we have lost the game today.
Concept to recallSorrow is expressed with the interjection Alas!
  1. ‘It is sad that’ → ‘Alas!’
  2. The others are ungrammatical or simply assertive with ‘!’.

Answer: option (4) — Alas! we have lost the game today.

Q858CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q29NTA final key
Change the following Assertive sentence into an Exclamatory sentenece.
She is a very intelligent child.
  1. What an intelligent child she!
  2. An intelligent child what she is!
  3. What an intelligent child!
  4. She must be an intelligent girl!
Concept to recall‘a very + adjective + noun’ → ‘What a(n) + adjective + noun + subject + verb!’
  1. The full form is ‘What an intelligent child she is!’
  2. Of the options, (1) keeps the subject she (as printed, the verb is is missing); (3) drops the subject altogether.
  3. (2) has the wrong order; (4) changes the meaning to a guess.

Answer: option (1) — What an intelligent child she!

NoteAs printed, (1) lacks ‘is’ and (3) is an acceptable elliptical exclamation; NTA’s final key gives (1), the option that keeps the subject.
Q859CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q34NTA final key
Choose an appropriate form of Greeting in an Informal letter, is :
  1. My Dear Mother
  2. Respected Sir,
  3. Dear Sir,
  4. The Most Reverend
Concept to recallInformal letters (to family/friends) greet by relation or name: ‘My dear Mother’.
  1. Sir/Respected Sir are formal; ‘The Most Reverend’ is a title for clergy.
  2. So ‘My Dear Mother’.

Answer: option (1) — My Dear Mother

Q860CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q35NTA final key
Courteous leave taking in a formal letter, is one among the following. Choose the appropriate option.
  1. Your Sincere Friend,
  2. Yours faithfully,
  3. Your Lovingly.
  4. with lot of Love
Concept to recallFormal close: ‘Yours faithfully,’.

Q861CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q45NTA final key
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) every where(I) adverb of manner
(B) completely(II) adverb of frequency
(C) consequently(III) adverb of place
(D) faithfully(IV) adverb of reason

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  2. (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
  3. (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
  4. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Concept to recalleverywhere = place; consequently = reason/result; faithfully = manner; completely = degree (the only type left here is ‘frequency’).
  1. Fix the sure ones: A-III (place), C-IV (reason), D-I (manner).
  2. Only option (2) has all three; it pairs B with II by elimination.

Answer: option (2) — (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

Q862CUET 2023 · 21 Jun, Shift 1 · Q46NTA final key
Fill in the blanks with an appropriate question tag.
Few people got the question right, _________?
  1. didn’t they
  2. couldn’t they
  3. did they
  4. can’t they
Concept to recallFew, little, hardly, seldom, never make a sentence negative, so the tag is positive.
  1. ‘Few people’ = almost no one → negative sense → positive tag.
  2. Past simple got → auxiliary did: ‘did they?’
